Boulkiemdé/Nanoro : la délégation spéciale tient sa 3e session ordinaire de l’année 2026
items.description: BURKINA-BOULKIEMDE-NANORO-CCC-SESSION-ORDINAIRE Boulkiemdé/Nanoro : la délégation spéciale tient sa 3e session ordinaire de l'année 2026 Nanoro, 24 août 2026 (AIB) — La commune de Nanoro a abrité lundi, dans la salle des fêtes de la mairie, les travaux de sa troisième session ordinaire de l'année 2026. Placée sous la présidence du préfet et Président de la délégation spéciale (PDS), Nourou Guiguimdé, cette rencontre a mobilisé les membres de l'organe délibérant autour des grands chantiers de développement local. L'ordre du jour de cette session s'articulait autour de trois axes majeurs notamment l'examen, l'amendement et l'adoption du procès-verbal de la deuxième session ordinaire ; l'étude et l'adoption d'une délibération cruciale portant sur l'autorisation d'ouverture de concours professionnels d'entrée à l'École Nationale d'Administration et de Magistrature (ENAM), session 2026 ; le suivi des opportunités offertes par l'Agence Nationale d'Appui au Développement des Collectivités Territoriales (ADCT), dans le cadre de l'octroi de cent bourses de formation aux collectivités territoriales. Au titre des informations et divers, le PDS a porté à la connaissance des participants la présence active d'une équipe du Centre National d'Assurance Maladie Universelle (CNAMU) dans la localité. Cette mission a pour mandat d'informer, sensibiliser et procéder à l'immatriculation des agents des secteurs public et privé ainsi que des acteurs du secteur informel, incitant l'ensemble de la population à s'enrôler massivement. En clôturant les travaux, le Camarade Guiguimdé a salué l'engagement des membres de la délégation spéciale pour leur assiduité et leurs contributions constructives. Il a également exprimé sa gratitude aux responsables du CNAMU pour la qualité des éclairages apportés sur le dispositif en cours. « Je remercie profondément les membres de la délégation spéciale qui ont répondu présents à cette session, les responsables du CNAMU qui nous ont éclairés, ainsi que tous les participants dont les apports nous ont permis de prendre des décisions pour le développement de notre commune », s'est-il réjoui. Agence d'Information du Burkina BB/PB/AS/ATA

Two killed as police, hoodlums clash in Ikire
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo OSOGBO — Two persons were reportedly killed in Ikire, Irewole Local Government Area of Osun State, following a clash between police personnel and hoodlums allegedly attempting to take control of a motor park and the local government secretariat. The incident occurred amid a warning by the state government on Sunday against attempts by individuals or groups to forcefully take over motor parks and local government secretariats, urging security agencies to remain vigilant and prevent any breakdown of law and order. Sources in Ikire said some hoodlums allegedly mobilised from the Oja-Ale area and moved towards Naira and Kobo, where they reportedly attempted to take over the motor park and the local government secretariat located along the expressway. A shop owner, who pleaded anonymity, said the hoodlums allegedly attacked an individual on reaching the area, prompting residents to alert the police. According to the source, police officers were subsequently deployed to the area. “The hoodlums dared the police and disarmed one of the officers, which led the Divisional Police Officer to reinforce his men at Naira and Kobo. “On getting there, the hoodlums and the police engaged in an exchange of gunfire, and we ran for safety. “Later, we discovered that two persons were hit by bullets around the expressway. We also heard that the police recovered the weapon seized by the hoodlums,” the source said. As of the time of filing this report, the Osun State Commissioner of Police was in Ikire conducting an on-the-spot assessment of the incident. The command’s spokesperson, DSP Abiodun Ojelabi, was also with the commissioner during the assessment. When contacted, Ojelabi said he would brief journalists after the completion of the assessment tour. The post Two killed as police, hoodlums clash in Ikire appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Extortion allegation serious; evidence must back claim – Edem Senanu
items.description: Anti-corruption campaigner Edem Senanu says the allegation of extortion against the Minority Leader is a serious matter that warrants investigation and must be supported by substantive evidence. His comments follow an allegation by the Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, against the Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin, which has triggered a public debate over the matter. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse , Mr Senanu explained that “extortionist” was not merely an insult but a technical term with a specific meaning. “If you say extortionist, it’s a technical term meaning that somebody is forcibly compelling you to give them money, resources, items, which is not their due. “So extortionist means something specific has happened, and it is worth proving and investigating whether something has happened outside the public view, which the Chief Executive of GoldBod is alluding to and that could have implications, so it is worthy of investigating and a serious issue,” he explained. He, however, emphasised the need for credible evidence to support the claim. “I’m hoping that if something like that has happened, there is substantive evidence that backs this particular allegation,” he said. Mr Senanu also referenced recent Ghana Statistical Service data indicating an increase in extortion involving public officers, arguing that the issue deserved attention and further scrutiny. He said an investigation could help establish what actually transpired and determine whether the allegation had any basis. Meanwhile, the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) says it is reviewing the allegation to establish whether it has the legal authority to investigate the matter.

items.title: Oyo govt accuses FG of politicising Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode road
items.description: By Adeola Badru IBADAN — The Oyo State Government has accused the Federal Government of politicising the flag-off of the reconstruction and dualisation of the Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode Road by excluding Governor Seyi Makinde from the ceremony. The project flag-off was held on Monday at Idi Ayunre in Oluyole Local Government Area of Oyo State, with the state government expressing displeasure over what it described as the deliberate exclusion of Makinde from an event concerning a major federal road project within the state. In a statement issued by the Oyo State Commissioner for Information, Prince Dotun Oyelade, the government described the governor’s exclusion as politically motivated and said it was difficult to separate the decision from the emerging political contest ahead of the 2027 elections. Oyelade said excluding Makinde from the ceremony amounted to taking partisan politics beyond acceptable limits, given the importance of the road project to Oyo State and the wider South-West region. He said the flag-off, attended by Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun, Minister of Works Dave Umahi, the All Progressives Congress governorship candidate, Sarafadeen Alli, and the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, fell short of the significance expected of such an important infrastructure event because of what he described as its political undertone. According to him, the decision demonstrated a lack of political sagacity and confidence on the part of those behind the arrangement. The commissioner particularly faulted the explanation that Makinde was not invited because he was on leave, arguing that the presence of an Acting Governor meant the state had adequate representation available for the event. Oyelade said Makinde’s absence from the state could therefore not reasonably have been used as justification for excluding the Oyo State Government from a major federal infrastructure event taking place within its territory. The commissioner said Makinde remained unperturbed by the development but regretted that an occasion that should have focused on the commencement of a strategically important road project had instead been reduced to what he described as a “political jamboree.” He maintained that the administration would not be distracted by the development, insisting that the people of Oyo State remained the ultimate stakeholders in the state’s political direction. “The course of 2027 is set, and no level of indecorum or desperation from whatever quarters will hold back the will of the people,” Oyelade said. The Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode Road is a major inter-state route linking Oyo and Ogun states and providing an important connection between Ibadan and the wider South-West corridor. The Oyo government’s reaction comes amid increasing political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections, with major political parties and their candidates already positioning themselves for the contests. The state government therefore viewed the exclusion of Makinde from Monday’s flag-off not merely as a protocol issue but as part of the wider political atmosphere surrounding the 2027 elections. The post Oyo govt accuses FG of politicising Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode road appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Championnats 1 et ligue 2: le démarrage de la saison prévu le 3 octobre
items.description: La Ligue sénégalaise de football professionnel (Lsfp) a tenu, samedi, son Assemblée générale ordinaire. Elle a profité de cette tribune pour dévoiler le calendrier de la phase aller du championnat professionnel (Ligue 1 et Ligue 2) saison 2026-2027 qui démarre le 3 octobre prochain. La succession de Teungueth Fc est ouverte. La Ligue sénégalaise de football professionnel (Lsfp) a dévoilé, samedi, au cours de son Assemblée générale ordinaire, le calendrier de la phase aller du championnat professionnel de Ligue 1. Champion du Sénégal en titre, Teungueth Fc aura à cœur de conserver sa couronne, mais c’est une mission qui s’annonce d’ores et déjà compliquée puisqu’il aura à faire à l’Us Ouakam à domicile dans un bouillant derby lébou. Comme si cela ne suffisait pas, Teungueth Fc va devoir enchaîner des chocs à partir de la 4e journée contre l’As Pikine (4e j), As Jaraaf (5e j), Diambars Fc (6e j), Us Gorée (7e j), Génération Foot (8e j) et Ajel (9e j). Un programme plus que corsé pour Teungueth Fc qui saura s’il sera en mesure de réaliser la passe de deux durant cette période. Son voisin et rival et par ailleurs son dauphin, Ajel, tentera, elle, de confirmer ses bonnes prédispositions montrées depuis son accession à l’élite. L’Us Gorée, pour sa part, aura une revanche à prendre, elle qui s’est fait larguer dans la course au titre sur les deux derniers exercices à chaque fois en fin de saison. Très attendu, le derby de la banlieue opposant Guédiawaye Fc à l’As Pikine est programmé pour la fin de la phase aller (15e j), bien après le duel des promus Essamaye Fc-Diambars Fc qui s’affronteront lors de la première journée. En Ligue 2, l’As Douanes tentera d’accrocher le train de la montée après plusieurs saisons infructueuses. Elle avait loupé la montée que d’un seul cheveu (1 point) et elle essaiera de repartir du bon pied lors de la réception de Jamono Fatick (1er j) alors que le Duc (4e du dernier exercice à 4 points du champion) reçoit Amitié Fc. Relégués à l’issue de la saison dernière, l’As Cambérène se frottera à Oslo Fa tandis que la Sonacos défiera Téranga Sc. Après plusieurs années en Nationale, l’Asfa retrouve le football professionnel avec beaucoup d’ambitions et une envie folle de faire la différence dès son entrée en lice contre l’As Kaffrine qui avait échappé de peu à la relégation (14e). Ayant fini tous les deux en milieu de tableau la saison dernière, As Saloum (6e) et Niarry Tally (7e) voudront lancer leur saison de la plus belle des manières en espérant faire partie des équipes qui mèneront la danse.

items.title: Quarante ans d’ordures, deux drames : plongée dans la décharge de Dar-es-salam devenue une bombe à retardement
items.description: À Dar-Es-Salam, l’histoire semble se répéter, avec une violence toujours plus grande. Ouverte dans les années 1980, la décharge devait pourtant n’être qu’une solution provisoire. Elle avait été dimensionnée pour une ville d’environ 500 000 habitants et sa durée de vie était fixée à vingt ans. Quatre décennies plus tard, elle continue d’engloutir les déchets d’une capitale qui compte désormais plusieurs millions d’habitants. À l’origine, le site de Dar-es-salam 2, également associé à La Minière ou au Concasseur, n’était pas destiné à devenir l’immense réceptacle des ordures de Conakry. La zone abritait notamment une carrière d’argile, exploitée pour divers usages artisanaux. Des excavations de plusieurs dizaines de mètres témoignent encore de cette ancienne activité. Le projet initial prévoyait la fermeture du site au bout de vingt ans et son transfert vers Kagbélén, dans la périphérie de Dubréka. Mais le calendrier n’a jamais été respecté. Le nouveau site n’a pas véritablement pris le relais et Dar-es-salam est resté en service, année après année, décennie après décennie. Entre-temps, des habitations se sont développées autour de la décharge. Des familles ont construit, loué, grandi et vécu à quelques mètres des montagnes d’immondices. Certaines ont même été contraintes de quitter leurs maisons lors des opérations de déguerpissement engagées autour du site. Le logement est ainsi devenu l’autre visage de cette crise : comment protéger les populations installées à proximité d’une décharge devenue dangereuse, tout en garantissant leurs droits et leur indemnisation ? Notre reportage grand format réalisé sur place en 2019 révélait déjà l’ampleur de cette fracture. https://guineenews.org/2020/ 06/15/gestion-des-dechets-a- conakry-au-coeur-de-la- decharge-sauvage-de-dar-es- salam-leternel-enfer-pour-les- riverains/?amp=1 Des familles affirmaient avoir été recensées, sans avoir reçu leurs compensations. D’autres avaient vu leurs maisons disparaître sous les engins. Le site, réduit par l’occupation humaine et la pression foncière, était alors passé d’environ 25 à 15 hectares. Et puis, il y a les drames. Le 22 août 2017, l’effondrement d’une partie de la décharge avait déjà endeuillé Dar-es-salam. Neuf personnes avaient perdu la vie, rappelant brutalement qu’une montagne de déchets n’est jamais un simple amas d’ordures : elle peut devenir un piège mortel pour les riverains, les récupérateurs et tous ceux qui s’en approchent. Mais, dimanche 23 août 2026, le cauchemar s’est reproduit à une tout autre échelle. Un nouvel éboulement a enseveli des personnes sous les déchets. Le bilan demeure encore évolutif, mais plus d’une cinquantaine de victimes sont concernées, entre morts, personnes ensevelies et disparus selon les informations disponibles, au moment de la rédaction de cet article. Les recherches se poursuivent, tandis que des familles attendent toujours des nouvelles de leurs proches. Neuf ans après le drame de 2017, Dar-es-salam rappelle donc une vérité que les chiffres ne peuvent plus masquer : la décharge n’est plus seulement un problème d’assainissement, elle est devenue une question de sécurité publique, de logement et de dignité humaine. Pendant des années, les autorités ont annoncé des projets de transfert, de modernisation et de traitement des déchets. Des financements ont été mobilisés, des opérateurs recrutés et des échéances annoncées. Mais Dar-es-salam est toujours là. Jusqu’à quand faudra-t-il attendre pour que la promesse d’une nouvelle solution ne soit plus une échéance repoussée de trois ans en trois ans ? Après 2017, fallait-il attendre 2026 pour comprendre que Dar-es-salam était une bombe à retardement ? Méditons-y !

items.title: Is Wontumi’s priority NPP chairmanship when in prison? – Kwasi Kwarteng asks campaign team
items.description: Lawyer and New Patriotic Party (NPP) communicator Kwasi Kwarteng has questioned the basis for the decision by the campaign team of National Chairman hopeful Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, to pick nomination forms on his behalf while he remains in custody. According to him, Wontumi’s immediate priority should be securing his freedom rather than contesting the NPP National Chairmanship race. Speaking on Adom FM’s Dwaso Nsem , Mr Kwarteng said the circumstances surrounding Wontumi’s incarceration raise questions about the purpose of picking the forms for him when his bail application is still pending. “You have applied for bail, and it is pending, while his lawyer is also having some issues with the judiciary. So what is the basis for picking the forms for who to vote for who?” he questioned. He argued that the fundamental effect of imprisonment is the loss of personal liberty and, therefore, Wontumi’s immediate concern should be regaining his freedom. “Wontumi’s priority now is not to become a chairman. His biggest priority is to gain his freedom, not chairmanship.” Mr Kwarteng questioned whether there was any established precedent that would allow a person in Wontumi’s current situation to go through the party’s vetting process, particularly if his participation would require special intervention. “Even if your government was in power, precedent will not allow it because who are you writing a letter to allow you to go for a vetting?” he asked. He said rather than focusing on the NPP chairmanship contest, Wontumi’s supporters should concentrate on lawful ways of helping Wontumi secure bail. “If we have something to do for him, it is for us to pray and use the right channels to secure his bail,” he said. Mr Kwarteng further questioned whether Wontumi himself would choose the chairmanship over his freedom if he were presented with such a choice. “Because even if a powerful man of God comes out today to say Wontumi stands a high chance of winning the chairmanship race but has to choose between that and his freedom, do you think it will be the chairmanship? For what?” He therefore urged the party and Wontumi’s supporters to exercise restraint in their actions and public commentary, warning that attempts to push ahead with the political contest could potentially affect the pending bail application. “His freedom is what matters, so they should exercise restraint and not prejudice the judge to spoil his chances on the bail,” he urged. Kwasi Kwarteng (PRO, Ministry of Education)_7 The decision of Chairman Wontumi’s team to pick nomination forms for him last week has sparked mixed reactions, with many describing it as misplaced. Executive Director and Head of Research at Global InfoAnalytics, Mussa Dankwah, for instance, has urged the NPP to focus on rebuilding its electoral fortunes ahead of the next general election rather than making a political statement by choosing a chairman who is serving a prison sentence. He further claimed that the NPP has already lost significant support among elite voters and warned that the party’s current approach could make it more difficult to win back that constituency.

items.title: OSP’s review of extortion allegation should not take more than a day – Edem Senanu
items.description: Anti-corruption campaigner Edem Senanu says the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) should not take more than a day to determine whether an extortion allegation involving the Minority Leader falls within its statutory mandate. His comments follow the OSP’s decision to review the allegations of extortion and related conduct made by the Chief Executive of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, against the Minority Leader of Parliament, Alexander Afenyo-Markin, to establish whether it has the legal authority to investigate the matter. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Monday, August 24, Mr Senanu said the OSP’s initial assessment should be completed quickly, given the nature of the allegation. “That shouldn’t take them more than a day. So strictly speaking, if they want to give us some information, I would expect that by tomorrow [Tuesday] OSP should get back to us, at the latest Wednesday, to say yes, this is within our mandate or not, and this is how we’re going to proceed,” he said. According to Mr Senanu, the OSP’s swift response to the allegation is a positive sign, particularly after months of limited public activity amid legal challenges involving the office. Mr Senanu urged the OSP to provide clarity on the matter promptly to prevent prolonged uncertainty surrounding the allegation.

items.title: Amotekun arrests suspected kidnapper negotiating ransom, another targeting ex-boss’s wife
items.description: —Parades 10 suspected criminals By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Ondo State Security Network Agency, codenamed Amotekun, has arrested two suspected kidnappers and eight other suspects for various offences across the state. Parading the suspects in Akure, the state Commander, Chief Adetunji Adeleye, said one of the suspected kidnappers, Gambo, 27, was arrested in Shasha while allegedly negotiating ransom with the families of his victims. Adeleye said Gambo was unaware that Amotekun operatives were monitoring the area and was subsequently apprehended behind Shasha in Akure. The second suspect, identified as Murtala, 19, was arrested with a locally made firearm and other weapons while allegedly attempting to kidnap the wife of his former employer in Molege, Owo. According to Adeleye, Murtala had gained entry into the woman’s residence but was foiled after the husband and neighbours raised the alarm. “They mobilised Amotekun and Fulani community members who cordoned off the area and successfully apprehended him,” he said. The commander said the suspect allegedly confessed to involvement in several kidnapping operations and admitted that the Owo incident was his latest target. Adeleye commended members of the Fulani community for assisting Amotekun in identifying suspected criminal elements among them. “The amazing part of this struggle is that the Fulani men who joined us were the ones who assisted in identifying the kidnappers among them, so that we would not generalise,” he said. He added that the second kidnap suspect also allegedly confessed to being a serial kidnapper operating around the Akure North axis. The commander said the eight other suspects were arrested for alleged burglary, motorcycle theft and other offences. He identified one of the suspects, Mustafa Aniliasu, as an alleged specialist in stealing motorcycles and burgling churches and mosques. His latest alleged operation, Adeleye said, was the burglary of a church in Elegbeka. Also paraded were Joseph, 25, and Friday, 20, who were arrested for allegedly stealing and reselling motorcycles. Adeleye said one of them kept a stolen motorcycle and later sold it for N70,000. Another suspect, Duyilemi, was arrested for allegedly posing as an Okada rider in the evening and robbing passengers at knifepoint before stealing their motorcycles. He was arrested in the Sango area of Akure North following a sting operation, the commander said. Wahab was arrested for allegedly stealing drum sets in Danjuma, along the Ondo Road, while Aminu, 28, was arrested for allegedly burgling a church in the Sijuade area. The last suspect, Kabiru, described by Adeleye as a suspected serial housebreaker, was arrested for allegedly stealing a gas cylinder. The commander said Kabiru had been arrested and released on bail several times. Adeleye said all the suspects would be handed over to the police for prosecution. items.title: Aiyedatiwa flags off 2.38km Akure flyover, says project necessary
items.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State on Monday flagged off the construction of a 2.38-kilometre flyover bridge in Akure, the state capital, describing the project as necessary to address growing traffic congestion and improve transportation in the metropolis. The project, which is the second flyover bridge being constructed in Akure, will run along the Oyemekun-Off Oba Adesida Road corridor, from Adegbola Junction to St. Matthias/NNPC Filling Station. Speaking at the flag-off ceremony, Aiyedatiwa said the project followed a detailed assessment by the Ministry of Infrastructure, Lands and Housing. He described the axis as one of the busiest arteries in the state capital, noting that it had become a major hub for commercial, administrative and social activities. “It has long served as the fulcrum of commercial, administrative and social activity in the capital city,” he said. “It connects our foremost markets, financial institutions and educational establishments, places of worship and dense residential settlements. It is the corridor through which the economic life of Akure passes daily. “Yet, with growth has come considerable strain. Increasing population, rising vehicular movement and expanding commercial activities have created persistent congestion and heightened the risk of road accidents. “These challenges hamper productivity, discourage investment and compromise the safety and well-being of our citizens. A responsible government must therefore act decisively to remedy the situation, and that is exactly what we are doing right now.” ‘Project more than necessary’ Responding to criticism over the construction of the flyover, Aiyedatiwa said the project was consistent with President Bola Tinubu’s position that flyovers should only be constructed where they were necessary. He urged critics not to quote the President out of context. “Let me quickly remind all of us, especially those naysayers that never see anything good in what we are doing. “This is not the kind of location Mr. President was referring to when he said governors should stop building flyovers. He said they should not erect them where they are unnecessary. You must add the other side of his speech. Do not quote Mr. President out of context. “Where it is necessary, you can do it. This one is more than necessary, and that is why we are doing it,” he said. The governor also thanked Tinubu for the Federal Government’s fiscal reforms, which he said had enabled states to access increased allocations from the Federation Account. “It is because we have the money that we are embarking on this project,” he said. Aiyedatiwa said the decision to construct the flyover was based on careful planning, critical appraisal and extensive stakeholder engagement. According to him, the project is designed to provide a modern transport solution that will improve the movement of people and goods across the metropolis. “Our objective is to deliver a modern transport solution that prioritises efficiency, safety and seamless movement of persons and goods within the metropolis. “Upon completion, we will ease congestion at critical points, particularly at Adegbola, Oba Adesida and Alagbaka. “It will shorten travel time for commuters, reduce vehicle operating costs and improve air quality by limiting idling in traffic,” he said. He added that the project would reposition Akure as a more competitive and investor-friendly capital by improving its infrastructure and creating an environment conducive to business growth. “More importantly, it will reposition Akure as a competitive and investor-friendly capital — a city with efficient infrastructure that attracts businesses, retains talent and expands opportunities for our youth,” he said. The governor stressed that infrastructure development must ultimately translate into improved living conditions for residents. “When traders at Oba Adesida Market can move their goods with ease, when students can get to school on time, when patients can reach hospitals without delay and when workers can return home after work with less stress, then we will have succeeded in translating policy into tangible benefits,” Aiyedatiwa said. He charged the contractor to execute the project according to specifications, budget and schedule, while maintaining high standards of professionalism and safety. Also speaking, the Commissioner for Infrastructure, Abiola Olawoye, urged the contractor to adhere strictly to the approved specifications and timelines. Olawoye also highlighted several road projects rehabilitated and constructed by the state government across Ondo State. The post Aiyedatiwa flags off 2.38km Akure flyover, says project necessary appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Investors received GH¢37bn in dividends, nearly GH¢800m in bond coupons – GSE MD
items.description: Investors in companies listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange received GH¢37 billion in dividends over the past 12 months, while investors in corporate bonds and commercial paper earned nearly GH¢800 million in coupon payments, Managing Director of the Ghana Stock Exchange, Abena Amoah, has disclosed. She said the figures demonstrate the growing role of Ghana’s capital market in creating wealth for investors while providing businesses with access to long-term financing. Ms Amoah disclosed this at the listing ceremony of Petrosol Platinum Energy PLC’s GH¢200 million note programme on the Ghana Fixed Income Market. According to Ms Amoah, investors who own shares in companies listed on the GSE have received substantial returns through dividend payments over the past year. “My equities team informs me that in the last 12 months, by way of dividends, investors have received GH¢37 billion in dividends in the last 12 months from companies listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange,” she said. She added that investors in corporate bonds and commercial paper received almost GH¢800 million in coupon payments during the same period. Ms Amoah said the figures highlight the capital market’s importance beyond its role in helping companies raise funds. “That shows the importance of our capital markets as an important tool for wealth generation,” she said. She explained that returns paid to investors can subsequently be reinvested, creating a cycle through which savings are channelled back into productive economic activities. The dividend payments represent returns to shareholders who own portions of listed companies, while the coupon payments are interest earned by investors who provide financing to businesses through debt instruments. The disclosure comes as the Ghana Stock Exchange continues to encourage more businesses to consider the capital market as an alternative to traditional bank financing. Ms Amoah said the exchange provides companies with several avenues for raising funds, including equities, corporate bonds, commercial paper, green bonds, and sustainable bonds. She said 15 corporate issuers have raised about GH¢24 billion through the corporate bond market since its establishment in 2015. She also pointed to Ghana’s pension funds, which she said manage more than GH¢120 billion in assets, as a significant source of capital that could support businesses seeking financing. Her message to businesses was straightforward: “The market is open. The capital is here.” The comments were made at the listing of Petrosol Platinum Energy PLC’s GH¢200 million note programme on the Ghana Fixed Income Market. The transaction provides the indigenous downstream petroleum company with longer-term financing while giving investors another opportunity to invest in corporate fixed-income securities. The listing adds to efforts to deepen Ghana’s corporate debt market and encourage more local businesses to raise capital domestically. For the GSE, the returns received by investors demonstrate that the capital market can serve both sides of the economy — providing businesses with funding to expand while giving savers and investors opportunities to earn returns. Ms Amoah is therefore urging more Ghanaian companies to tap into the market as the exchange seeks to expand the role of domestic capital in financing economic growth.

items.title: Tunisie : manifestations de colère après le naufrage d’une embarcation de migrants
items.description: Drame en Tunisie. Quinze migrants ont pris place, mercredi dernier, dans une embarcation de fortune censée les mener vers les côtes européennes. Un seul est revenu vivant ! Une fin tragique les attendait cependant au large de Zarzis dans le Sud-Est du pays. Un drame qui provoque la colère en Tunisie. Après avoir quitté la région de Zarzis, l’embarcation a mis le cap vers l'île italienne de Lampedusa, à 145 km de son point de départ. Mais dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi, et après environ 5 heures de navigation, l’eau commençait à s'infiltrer à bord, raconte le seul rescapé au média tunisien La Presse . Tunisie : 15 migrants partent vers l’Italie, un seul survivant Il précise que le navire n’a pas tardé à couler et qu’il avait passé deux jours à nager dans l’espoir de rester en vie. Il a été le seul à être secouru par un navire libyen qui passait par là. 12 corps ont été ensuite repêchés sans vie, tandis que les deux autres passagers de cette embarcation demeurent introuvables. Si l’unique survivant attribue ce drame à la surcharge de l’embarcation, la jeunesse de Ben Guerdane dans la région de Zarzis, d’où sont issus les migrants, a laissé exploser sa colère et réclame une enquête sur les causes du drame. Des manifestations ont vite dégénéré en affrontements avec les forces de l’ordre, samedi soir, dans la ville de Ben Guerdane. Les manifestants demandent aux autorités de décréter une journée de deuil national et d’enquêter sur cette affaire, rapporte Info Migrants . Des dizaines de manifestants ont lancé des jets de pierres sur les forces de l’ordre et ont allumé des brasiers en pleine rue pour demander aux autorités d’accélérer les opérations de recherche et de sauvetage, rapporte BBC Arabic. Voir cette publication sur Instagram Une publication partagée par BBC News عربي (@bbcarabic) Drame au large de Zarzis : la faute à qui ? Le Forum démocratique pour le travail et les libertés, parti d’opposition en Tunisie, a publié un communiqué où il rappelle que ce genre de drames est souvent « le résultat d’une économie qui n’offre pas d’espoir, engendrant chômage, marginalisation et manque de perspectives ». Pour le président de l'Observatoire tunisien des droits de l'homme, Mostafa Abdelkebir, la Tunisie ne fait que « payer le prix de politiques européennes inhumaines et injustes » qui forcent les migrants à choisir des routes de plus en plus dangereuses. Il est à rappeler que la Tunisie a signé en 2023, avec le gouvernement italien , un accord de plus de 250 millions d’euros, afin de lutter contre l’immigration clandestine. L’article Tunisie : manifestations de colère après le naufrage d’une embarcation de migrants est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: À Paris, le Bourd rassemble les fidèles autour de l’héritage de Tivaouane
items.description: À Paris, cette année encore, la communauté tidiane de France, l’une des plus dynamiques de la diaspora, s’est mobilisée pendant les dix jours du Bourd pour vibrer au rythme de la ferveur spirituelle du Mawloudou Nabi, à l’initiative de la Zawiya Seydina Cheikh de Paris. Des centaines de fidèles issus des différentes dahiras d’Île-de-France se sont rassemblés chaque jour depuis l’ouverture du Bourd à Tivaouane, marquant le début des célébrations de la naissance du Sceau des Prophètes, Seydina Mouhamed (PSL). En France, comme partout ailleurs en Europe, l’héritage spirituel de Tivaouane demeure un rendez-vous à ne pas manquer. Cette dynamique a été initiée sous l’impulsion des guides religieux. Serigne Abdoul Aziz Sy Al Amine avait notamment appelé les responsables à faire de l’unité leur maître-mot, à organiser collectivement les Burds et le Gamou en s’inspirant de Tivaouane, et à œuvrer à l’acquisition d’une Zawiya à Paris. Quinze ans après les premiers Burds collectifs, cette recommandation se poursuit avec un objectif clair : offrir aux générations présentes et futures un lieu durable de prière, de transmission et de rassemblement. À travers cette mobilisation, la communauté tidiane de France entend ainsi préserver le lien spirituel avec Tivaouane et transmettre aux nouvelles générations l’héritage religieux qui continue de rayonner au-delà des frontières du Sénégal. Aïmirou SAMBE Coordonnateur du Projet ZAWIYA SEYDINA CHEIKH DE PARIS

items.title: Ogogo was cultural ambassador who elevated Yoruba traditions, values — Gani Adams
items.description: By Dapo Akinrefon The Aare Ona Kakanfo of Yorubaland, Iba Gani Adams, has described the late veteran actor, Taiwo Hassan, popularly known as Ogogo, as a cultural ambassador who used his craft to promote and preserve Yoruba traditions and values. Adams, in a condolence statement on Monday, expressed profound sorrow over the death of the actor, describing his contributions to the Yoruba film industry as remarkable and enduring. Hassan died on August 23, 2026, at the age of 66 after a battle with stage-four cancer, leaving a significant void in the Nigerian entertainment industry and Yoruba cultural community. Adams extended his condolences to the late actor’s family, friends, colleagues and fans, as well as the entire Yoruba film industry. He commended Ogogo’s dedication to promoting Yoruba heritage through his performances, which endeared him to audiences across Nigeria and beyond. According to him, the late actor distinguished himself through professionalism, versatility and an unwavering commitment to the arts. He said Ogogo’s legacy would continue to inspire generations of actors and theatre practitioners who regarded him as a role model. In the condolence message, Adams said, “Ogogo’s life and work exemplify the spirit of Yoruba artistry and the power of storytelling to unite and uplift our people.” He also sympathised with theatre practitioners and members of the entertainment industry over the loss, urging them to remain resilient in the face of the tragedy. Adams emphasised the importance of unity and collective prayers for the repose of Ogogo’s soul and called on Yoruba sons and daughters to rally around the deceased’s family. He prayed that the Almighty would grant the actor eternal rest and provide strength and comfort to his family and all those mourning him. Adams described Ogogo as a towering figure in the Nigerian film industry, particularly Yoruba-language cinema, whose career spanned several decades. He noted that the actor delivered memorable performances that left an enduring impression on audiences. According to him, Ogogo’s work went beyond entertainment, as he also helped educate audiences and preserve the rich cultural heritage of the Yoruba people. “Throughout his career, Ogogo was celebrated for his ability to portray a wide range of characters with depth and authenticity. His dedication to his craft earned him respect and admiration from colleagues, critics and fans alike. “Beyond his artistic talents, he was known for his humility, kindness and mentorship of younger actors, helping to nurture the next generation of Yoruba film stars,” the statement added. items.title: Cour d’Appel de Ouagadougou: 4 sessions d’audiences foraines pour rapprocher la Cour des citoyens à Bobo
items.description: La Cour administrative d’appel de Ouagadougou a ouvert, ce lundi 24 août 2026 à Bobo-Dioulasso, une série de quatre sessions d’audiences foraines, en présence d’autorités administratives et judiciaires ainsi que de nombreux citoyens. Cette initiative, selon l’écrit du ministère de la Justice, traduit «la volonté des autorités nationales de rapprocher davantage la justice des citoyens et de faciliter l’accès au service public de la justice». Au cours de ces audiences, «plus d’une centaine de recours seront examinés». En délocalisant ainsi ses activités, la Cour administrative d’appel entend «apporter une réponse concrète à l’engorgement des dossiers et contribuer à une justice plus accessible, plus diligente et plus proche des réalités des justiciables». Prévues jusqu’au 18 septembre 2026 au Tribunal administratif de Bobo-Dioulasso, ces audiences foraines illustrent l’engagement de la justice administrative à renforcer sa proximité avec les populations. Par Wakat Séra L’article Cour d’Appel de Ouagadougou: 4 sessions d’audiences foraines pour rapprocher la Cour des citoyens à Bobo est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Nigeria joins 2 other countries in exclusive World Cup group
items.description: Nigeria’s Falconets are set to achieve a remarkable feat at the 2026 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup, becoming one of only three countries to have featured in every edition of the tournament since its inception. The Nigerian side will join Brazil and the United States as the only nations with a perfect attendance record when the 2026 tournament gets underway in Poland. The competition is scheduled to take place from September 5 to 27, 2026, with the tournament expanding to 24 teams for the first time. Nigeria have participated in all 11 previous editions of the competition, which was originally launched as the FIFA U-19 Women’s World Championship in 2002 before being upgraded to the U-20 category in 2006. The Falconets made their debut at the inaugural tournament in Canada in 2002 but were eliminated at the group stage. They subsequently reached the quarter-finals in 2004 and 2006 before making further progress in later editions. Nigeria’s best performances came in 2010 and 2014, when they finished as runners-up. In 2010, the Falconets lost 2-0 to hosts Germany in the final, while they suffered a narrow 1-0 defeat to the same opponents after extra time in the 2014 final in Canada. The 2014 campaign also marked the emergence of former Falconets star Asisat Oshoala, who won both the Golden Ball and Golden Boot after an outstanding tournament. Nigeria finished fourth in 2012 and have since recorded quarter-final appearances in 2018 and 2022. They reached the Round of 16 in 2024, while their 2016 campaign in Papua New Guinea ended in the group stage. Across their 11 previous appearances, the Falconets have played 48 matches, recording 22 wins, 10 draws and 16 defeats, while scoring 77 goals. At the 2026 edition, Nigeria will compete in Group F alongside Spain, China PR and New Caledonia. With their historic attendance record already secured, the Falconets will be aiming to go a step further in Poland and win Nigeria’s first FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup title. items.title: Poutine reçoit le ministre indien des Affaires étrangères et met en avant le renforcement de la coopération russo-indienne
items.description: Vladimir Poutine a recu le 24 août au Kremlin le ministre indien des Affaires etrangeres, Subrahmanyam Jaishankar, pour examiner les principaux dossiers de la cooperation russo-indienne. Le president russe a notamment releve la reprise des echanges commerciaux en 2026 et confirme la volonte de Moscou d'accroître ses livraisons d'engrais a l'Inde. La rencontre a eu lieu apres une reunion de la commission intergouvernementale russo-indienne, dont Jaishankar preside la partie indienne et le premier vice-Premier ministre, Denis Mantourov, la partie russe. Des discussions avec le ministre russe des Affaires etrangeres Sergueï Lavrov figuraient egalement au programme. Au Kremlin, Poutine a insiste sur la continuite des relations entre les deux pays, developpees depuis plusieurs decennies. « Votre visite aujourd'hui souligne le niveau des relations qui se sont etablies entre la Russie et l'Inde depuis des decennies », a-t-il declare. Il a ajoute que Moscou et New Delhi poursuivaient leur cooperation « pratiquement dans tous les domaines », aux niveaux gouvernemental, parlementaire et economique. Apres un leger recul en 2025, le commerce bilateral est reparti a la hausse cette annee. Poutine a egalement souligne l'implication personnelle de Narendra Modi dans le developpement des relations avec Moscou. Cette progression s'accompagne d'une hausse des livraisons russes d'engrais, que la Russie se dit prete a renforcer afin de repondre aux besoins du secteur agricole indien. En 2025, elle etait devenue le premier fournisseur d'engrais de l'Inde. Nucleaire, technologies et projets industriels Le partenariat se developpe egalement dans le nucleaire et les hautes technologies. Denis Mantourov a notamment evoque la possibilite de localiser en Inde la production de combustible nucleaire, illustrant l'elargissement de la cooperation technologique entre les deux pays. Cette cooperation prend aussi une forme concrete dans les transports. Un prototype du train electrique rapide Vande Bharat, developpe dans le cadre d'un projet russo-indien, doit etre assemble dans l'etat du Maharashtra avant la fin de l'annee. Sa production en serie doit commencer apres les essais. Le projet repose sur un contrat remporte en 2023 par un consortium dirige par le groupe russe Transmashholding. Il prevoit la production et la maintenance de 1 920 voitures, donnant une dimension industrielle importante au partenariat entre Moscou et New Delhi. Poutine et Modi maintiennent des contacts reguliers Le developpement economique s'accompagne de contacts politiques reguliers au plus haut niveau. Jaishankar a transmis a Vladimir Poutine les salutations de Narendra Modi ainsi qu'un message de sa part. Le chef de la diplomatie indienne a indique que Modi attendait sa prochaine rencontre avec le president russe dans le cadre de l'Organisation de cooperation de Shanghai. Il a egalement exprime l'espoir de voir Vladimir Poutine participer au prochain sommet des BRICS organise en Inde. De son cote, Poutine a confirme son intention de rencontrer prochainement Narendra Modi et n'a pas exclu une nouvelle entrevue avant la fin de l'annee. Ces echanges reguliers accompagnent le developpement d'un partenariat russo-indien deja etendu au commerce, a l'energie, a l'agriculture, au nucleaire, aux transports et aux hautes technologies.

items.title: Tinubu links N296bn Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode road to 2027 stakes
items.description: By Adeola Badru IBADAN — President Bola Tinubu has linked the N296 billion reconstruction and dualisation of the 56.5-kilometre Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode road to his administration’s efforts to boost economic integration, regional trade and infrastructure-led development in the South-West. Tinubu spoke on Monday at the flag-off of the project at the Idi Ayunre end of the highway in Ibadan, Oyo State, where he also announced further Federal Government interventions on major roads across the region. The project, awarded to JRB Construction Limited following approval by the Federal Executive Council, is expected to improve connectivity between Oyo and Ogun states and strengthen access to the Lagos-Ogun economic corridor. Represented at the ceremony by Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun, the President said the project was part of his administration’s infrastructure agenda aimed at easing transportation challenges and improving the nation’s road network. He said the Federal Government was committed to making roads across the 36 states motorable, stressing that the Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode road was too strategically important to be neglected. “Today demonstrates the flag-off of the 56.5km Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode road. It is more than just a flag-off; it is a connection between the two states economically. “Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode is too important for the Federal Government to neglect. The importance of this road extends beyond the boundaries of the states,” Tinubu said. The President noted that the highway had for decades served farmers, manufacturers, students and other residents, adding that its reconstruction demonstrated the Federal Government’s commitment to providing safer roads. “For decades, farmers, manufacturers, students and other residents have depended on the use of this road. This project reflects the commitment of the Federal Government to delivering safer roads for the people of the country,” he said. Tinubu said the road had remained in poor condition despite its importance to several agrarian communities along the route. He added that its completion would boost the Gross Domestic Product of the benefiting states and create opportunities for increased local and foreign investment. The President directed the contractor to ensure that the project was delivered according to schedule. According to the Federal Government, the project will improve the capacity of the corridor, facilitate the movement of people and goods, and strengthen economic activities between Oyo and Ogun states. More roads for South-West In his remarks, the Minister of Works, Engr. Dave Umahi, disclosed that Tinubu had expanded the Federal Government’s intervention in the South-West with the approval for the reconstruction of the Ibadan-Abeokuta road and other federal highways. “Mr President directed me to act on the letter written by Oba Ladoja on the need for infrastructural development in the South-West region, which includes the Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode road and other roads in the region. “Also, Mr President has directed the reconstruction of Ibadan-Abeokuta road and 15 other roads in the region,” Umahi said. He said several roads had also been redesigned, including the Ibadan-Ife-Ilesha road, as part of the administration’s broader intervention in federal highways. “Every road that President builds has a lifespan of 109 years. Many roads have been redesigned, including Ibadan-Ife-Ilesha and others,” he said. However, Umahi acknowledged that the scale of the infrastructure programme meant some projects might not be completed before the end of the current administration in 2027. “We may not complete all the projects that we have started by 2027, but all will be completed and commissioned on or before 2031,” he said. Also speaking, the Minister of State for Works, Bello Mohammed, said the Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode project would ease transportation challenges confronting residents of the two states and demonstrate the Federal Government’s commitment to infrastructure development nationwide. He said the infrastructure programme covered the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. Mohammed, however, appealed to residents of the region to reciprocate the administration’s efforts with electoral support in 2027. “The only way to reciprocate the gesture is for the people in the region to vote massively for Tinubu and all the candidates of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in 2027,” he said. Ladoja seeks support for Tinubu In his address, the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, also linked the Federal Government’s intervention to support for Tinubu. Ladoja thanked the President for approving the project, recalling his earlier engagement with the Federal Government over infrastructure and security concerns in the region. “Tinubu deserves to be President since a long time. We appreciate him for making the road project possible, having known about insecurity on the road,” he said. He also recalled leading other Oyo State traditional rulers to meet Tinubu to express appreciation over the rescue of victims of the Oriire abductions. Ladoja said the road would strengthen relations between the Ibadan and Ijebu people while addressing security and transportation challenges along the corridor. “This road is going to improve the relationship between the Ijebu and Ibadan people. I have been assured that the road will be delivered in 24 months,” he said. The post Tinubu links N296bn Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode road to 2027 stakes appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 100 days after, where are the 44 missing Borno schoolchildren?
items.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri On the 15th of May 2026, some armed Boko Haram terrorists invaded Mussa Central Primary School in Askira-Uba Local Government Area of Southern Borno Senatorial District . They abducted over 40 schoolchildren, including a toddler. Similar incident also took place on 29th June, 2026 in Lassa community in the same council, where over 30 students of Technical College were also abducted. And since, there whereabouts are unknown. Due to the Renewed Boko Haram onslaught, the Borno State Government ordered for immediate closure of the two affected schools, where it moved the remaining students/pupils to a safer schools in Uba town. Last week, some parents of the abducted children from Mussa took to the streets in Askira-Uba Council Headquarters and protested. They later moved down to Maiduguri, the state capital to meet with Governor Babagana Umara Zulum, after their children had spent 100 days in captivity. During the meeting, Governor Zulum disclosed that the Federal Government and Borno State Government are working closely to ensure the safe rescue of schoolchildren abducted from Mussa community in Askira/Uba Local Government Area. Zulum expressed the deep sympathy of the Tinubu-led Federal Government and reiterated the President’s personal commitment to ensuring the children are safely returned to their families. Govt’s assurances He assured the parents that, under President Bola Tinubu, the Federal Government, the Nigerian Armed Forces, and Borno State Government will do everything possible to secure the children’s release. “On behalf of the government and people of Borno State, I once again extend my sympathies over what happened at Mussa Central Primary School on the 15th of May 2026 that led to the abduction of about 44 primary school pupils,” Zulum said. “Also, on behalf of the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Bola Tinubu, I want to sympathise with you. I want to assure you that Mr. President has since directed security agencies to ensure the rescue of our children. And I believe they are working to ensure their rescue,” he stated. The meeting was attended by the Senator representing Southern Borno, Mohammed Ali Ndume; Acting Chief of Staff to the Governor, Dr Babagana Mustapha Mallumbe; Commissioners for Education, Engr Lawan Abba Wakilbe; Commissioner for Inter-Governmental Affairs and Special Duties, Dr Samaila Abdulaziz Satumari, and the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Environment, Dr Juliana Bitrus. Ndume seeks renewed Military effort to rescue abducted Mussa, Lassa schoolchildren Senator Ndume has called on the Nigerian military to intensify efforts towards the rescue of victims abducted from communities across Southern Borno, including the schoolchildren from Mussa and Lassa, passengers abducted along the Buratai axis and the remaining victims from Ngoshe. Ndume made the appeal during a visit to the Theatre Command, North East ‘Operation HADIN KAI’, where he commended the Nigerian military under the Theatre Commander, Major General Abdulsalam Abubakar for its sustained efforts in combating insurgency and restoring relative peace across the region. Ndume, who is also a member of the Senate Committee on Army, said his visit was both to appreciate the military and to draw renewed attention to the plight of families whose loved ones remain in captivity. “Most importantly, General, I know you are putting in your best efforts towards the rescue of our children in Mussa and Lassa, the passengers abducted along the Buratai axis and the remaining victims from Ngoshe. “We know you are making efforts. But because of the anxiety we all share and the length of time these people have remained away from their families, I have to continue to push for greater effort,” Ndume said. He noted that some of the victims have now spent more than 100 days away from their families, creating deep anxiety among relatives and communities. According to the Senator, the appeal should not be interpreted as a failure to recognise the sacrifices and efforts of the military, but rather as a reflection of the responsibility of a representative to continue speaking for his people and demanding action where necessary. “Like Oliver Twist, I have come to ask for more for my people. It is my moral obligation to commend you when you do well and also bring the concerns of my constituents before you,” he said. Ndume said the security situation in Borno had improved significantly compared to previous years, attributing the progress to the sacrifices of officers and soldiers operating across the theatre. He commended the military coordination and synergy among the security agencies, describing it as a major factor behind the gains recorded in the fight against insurgency. The Senator also praised the improved relationship between the military and civilians, saying it has given communities greater confidence in the security forces and encouraged cooperation in the ongoing campaign against insurgency. He urged the military to sustain the momentum and intensify operations towards locating and safely reuniting all remaining abductees with their families. The lawmaker conveyed his appreciation, on behalf of the people of Borno South, to the Chief of Army Staff, Service Chiefs, theatre commander, officers and soldiers for their sacrifices. While thanking them for the progress recorded so far, Ndume maintained that the rescue of every remaining abductee must remain a priority. “The people are anxious, and the families are waiting. We appreciate what the military is doing, but we will continue to appeal for greater efforts until our people are reunited with their families,” the Senator said. Theatre Commander’s words Responding, the Theatre Commander, Major General Abubakar thanked Senator Ndume for the visit, and assured him that the concerns raised over the abducted victims had been noted. The commander reiterated the commitment of the Nigerian Army and other security agencies to ongoing operations aimed at protecting communities, stabilising affected areas and ensuring the safe return of residents displaced by years of insurgency. He attributed the successes being recorded in the theatre to the support of the Chief of Army Staff, Lt. General Waidi Shaibu, whom he said has a deep understanding of the operational environment in the North-East. According to him, the military has continued to expand its presence across vulnerable areas through the establishment of new formations, deployment of additional troops and strengthening of existing sectors. The Theatre Commander assured Senator Ndume that the military remains committed to improving security across Borno South, particularly in areas that have experienced repeated attacks and abductions. He said the government deserves recognition for supporting the military. He stressed that well-motivated and properly equipped troops are essential to winning the fight against insecurity. … on captives’ return On measure put in place to ensure safe return and captives, he said the current Chief of Army Staff, Lt. General Waidi Shaibu having previously served in the theatre, possessed a deep understanding of the operational environment and security challenges in the North-East. According to Abubakar, the establishment of new battalions and the deployment of troops to strategic locations have significantly improved security and restored social and economic activities in previously threatened communities. Major-General Abubakar disclosed that battalions in Mandaragrau and Kirawa are among the newly established military formations, with troops now physically deployed on the ground. “Previously, much of the military activity around some of these areas was conducted from across the Cameroon side. But today, we have soldiers physically deployed on the ground, and this has encouraged the return of socio-economic activities,” he said. Security steps The Theatre Commander further explained that a new Sector IV was created to cover Southern Borno and Northern Adamawa, with the objective of bridging the security gap between the two areas. He said the Chief of Army Staff had approved two additional battalions — 226 and 247 Battalions — to strengthen operations within the sector. “The two battalions are now fully functional, and going forward, you will see serious improvement in the security situation, particularly around the Chibok and Askira-Uba axis,” he assured. The commander also disclosed that the military was intensifying stabilisation operations to enable displaced persons and residents of communities affected by insurgency to safely return to their homes. He said the stabilisation efforts were being supported by strong collaboration between the military and the Borno State Government. The Theatre Commander assured that the concerns raised regarding the need for additional troops in Ngulde, Shaffa, Mandaragrau, Askira-Uba, Ngoshe and Kirawa had been noted. He also disclosed that the Nigerian Army was expecting the delivery of more than 20 additional operational platforms before the end of the year as part of ongoing efforts to strengthen military operations. He reassured the Senator that Borno South would continue to receive the necessary attention. “Be rest assured that your senatorial district will be safe and adequately covered,” the Theatre Commander said. items.title: Amelley Djosu: PR is not propaganda; Ghana’s music industry needs a professional reset
items.description: There is a strange thing happening in Ghana’s entertainment industry. We have become very good at making noise about our artists, but increasingly poor at managing the reputations we claim to be protecting. In some corners of the music industry, public relations has become a competition over who can clap back the hardest, trend the longest, insult a rival most creatively or manufacture the most flattering version of reality. The loudest publicist gets noticed. The most aggressive social media handler gets celebrated. The person with the sharpest tongue is sometimes treated as though they must also be the best communicator. Somewhere in all that noise, however, the actual practice of public relations is getting lost. This is not an attack on Ghanaian music publicists as a collective. There are excellent communications professionals working quietly behind the scenes, building relationships with journalists, positioning artists, managing crises, developing narratives and protecting reputations without making themselves the story. The problem is that the loudest examples are increasingly setting the standard, and that should concern anyone who cares about the future of Ghana’s creative industry. PR is supposed to protect reputation, not manufacture reality At its core, public relations is about reputation, relationships and understanding. The Chartered Institute of Public Relations defines PR as the planned and sustained effort to establish and maintain goodwill and mutual understanding between an organisation and its publics. It describes reputation as the result of what an organisation does, what it says and what others say about it. Importantly, the CIPR also stresses that effective PR requires listening and understanding, not simply broadcasting information. That definition is important because it tells us what PR is not. It is not lying, propaganda, abusing journalists because they published something unflattering, mobilising a fan army to attack another artist or creating a fictitious version of events because the truth does not look good enough. The Public Relations Society of America similarly places honesty, accuracy, independence, loyalty and fairness among the profession’s core values. Its code requires practitioners to be honest and accurate in their communications and to correct erroneous information for which they are responsible. The British CIPR is equally explicit. Its current code requires members to maintain professional integrity, deal honestly and fairly with clients, colleagues and the public, and uphold the reputation of the PR profession. Its guidance on accuracy says information given to journalists or others should be truthful and reasonably verified, and that practitioners should not omit or obscure information in a way that creates a misleading impression. So when did being a good PR person become synonymous with being the best defender of an artist at all costs? The fan army has changed the game Ghana’s music industry already operates within an intensely polarised fan culture. Bhim Nation, Shatta Movement, SarkNation, High Grade Family and other fan communities have become powerful digital ecosystems. They can mobilise quickly, amplify songs, sell tickets, defend an artist and create extraordinary visibility. That power is not inherently bad. Passionate fan communities are valuable assets for artists, and every major music market has them. The problem begins when professional communicators start behaving like fan soldiers. A publicist should be able to defend an artist without becoming indistinguishable from the artist’s most aggressive fan. That distinction matters because the moment a communications professional begins insulting another artist, mocking supporters or deliberately provoking a rival fan base, they are no longer simply managing communication. They are contributing to the very toxicity that makes the industry harder to navigate. And once the publicist becomes part of the fight, who is managing the reputation? This became particularly visible around awards season. The race for the Telecel Ghana Music Awards’ Artist of the Year has increasingly generated a parallel communications battle, with publicists and representatives making cases for their respective artists across radio, television and social media. A 2025 analysis of the TGMA race described the publicists behind King Paluta, Stonebwoy and King Promise as prominent voices shaping the contest and noted that some of their exchanges had become heated. Another commentary from Graphic Online argued that the debates sometimes resembled political contests in which communicators appeared to be trying to dominate or outdo one another. There is nothing wrong with campaigning. Strategic awards campaigning is a legitimate part of the entertainment business, particularly when an artist has a strong factual case to make. But there is a difference between presenting a compelling case for your client and attempting to discredit everyone standing in their way. The first is advocacy. The second can quickly become insecurity disguised as strategy. We are confusing visibility with competence Perhaps one of the biggest problems is that social media has distorted how we measure PR professionals. A communicator with 50,000 followers can look more influential than someone with 5,000 carefully cultivated media relationships. A publicist who trends every weekend can appear more effective than one whose work rarely becomes visible because it is happening behind the scenes. But PR is not a popularity contest. The best publicist may not be the person tweeting the most. They may be the person who knows which journalist to call early in the morning, which story should be addressed before it becomes a headline, which interview the artist should decline, which controversy requires a statement and which one should simply be ignored. They may be the person sitting in a management meeting saying, “No, we should not put this out.” That is PR too. In some situations, the most valuable thing a publicist does is stop their client from speaking. The professional value of PR goes far beyond press mentions. The CIPR identifies media relations, stakeholder relations, crisis and issues management, copywriting, editing and management of people and resources among the core tasks of modern PR professionals. That is a much bigger job than being the person who wins an argument online. A crisis is where the real professional is revealed This is where the recent conversation around Stonebwoy’s BHIM Festival concert at OVO Arena Wembley becomes instructive. The August 15, 2026 performance was a significant moment for Ghanaian music. OVO Arena Wembley describes it as the first time a Ghanaian artiste had headlined the iconic London venue, while subsequent Ghanaian media reports described the event as a sold out 12,500 capacity show. The achievement itself is significant. A Ghanaian artist taking a self-produced headline show to one of London’s major indoor entertainment venues is exactly the kind of international progress the industry should be celebrating. But the conversation quickly shifted after photographs and videos showed curtains covering sections of the arena. Questions followed online about the venue’s actual attendance and what “sold out” meant in that context. There are legitimate reasons why sections of a large arena might be closed or curtained. Production configuration, acoustics, sight-lines, lighting, ticket inventory and audience concentration can all influence how a venue is configured. Commentary following the event offered some of these explanations, including the argument that curtains can help create a more intimate atmosphere and improve acoustics. That is precisely why the communications response should be calm, factual and precise. Headlining a 12,500-capacity venue is not automatically the same thing as selling 12,500 tickets. Those are different claims. If the available ticket inventory was limited to a smaller configuration, explain it. If sections were closed for production or venue management reasons, explain that. If every ticket made available for sale was sold, provide the number. If there is a discrepancy between what was initially communicated and what the evidence appears to show, acknowledge it and clarify. None of these explanations diminishes the achievement. In fact, transparency could make the achievement stronger. The temptation in entertainment PR is often to make an accomplishment sound bigger than it already is. But a credible achievement does not need unnecessary inflation. A major Ghanaian artist performing at OVO Arena Wembley is a story worth telling on its own. That is the PR lesson. You do not protect a reputation by asking people to believe what the available evidence does not support. You protect it by giving people a credible account of what happened. The best PR people know when not to fight This is something the Ghanaian creative industry needs to learn. Not every criticism deserves a response. Not every tweet deserves a quote tweet. Not every rival needs to be answered, and not every negative story requires a counterattack. Sometimes silence is strategy. Sometimes clarification is enough. Sometimes you need to admit that something went wrong. Sometimes the smartest response is simply to provide the facts and move on. Music Business Worldwide recently profiled veteran music communications executive Andy Saunders, whose approach to crisis management begins with a basic question: “Did you do it?” Saunders explained that he needs to be confident his client is telling him the truth because without the truth, he cannot properly manage the crisis. That should be compulsory thinking for anyone working in artist PR. Before crafting the statement, find out what happened. Before defending the artist, ask the difficult questions. Before telling journalists something, verify it. Before posting, consider whether the statement will still look credible five years from now because the internet remembers. Your artist’s reputation is not the only reputation at stake There is another issue we rarely discuss. Every time a PR professional knowingly puts questionable information into the public domain, they are also spending their own professional credibility. Artists change management teams. Labels change. Managers leave. Publicists move from one client to another. Relationships end and careers evolve. But screenshots remain. Old interviews remain. Press statements remain. Tweets remain. Videos remain. The publicist who spends years defending questionable claims on behalf of one artist may eventually leave that camp and apply for another communications role. A future employer, client or collaborator can search their name and find the same material. That is the digital footprint. You may think you are protecting the artist today, but you could be damaging your own professional reputation tomorrow. This is why professional independence matters. A good publicist is loyal to the client, but loyalty does not mean surrendering professional judgement. The PRSA framework places loyalty alongside honesty, independence and fairness, while the CIPR expects practitioners to exercise professional judgement with integrity and accuracy. Your job is not simply to tell your client what they want to hear. Your job is to tell them what they need to hear. Sometimes that means saying, “We need to apologise.” Sometimes it means saying, “That claim cannot be substantiated.” Sometimes it means saying, “Do not respond.” Sometimes it means telling an artist, “You are wrong.” That is not betrayal. That is professional counsel. Ghana needs fewer digital warriors and more strategic communicators There is an uncomfortable irony here. We keep saying Ghana’s music industry needs to become more professional, yet we sometimes reward precisely the behaviour that undermines professionalism. We celebrate the person who “finished” another camp online. We praise the publicist who produces the most savage response. We mistake virality for effectiveness. We count followers instead of relationships and measure noise instead of outcomes. Meanwhile, a genuinely skilled communicator who prefers strategy, diplomacy and facts can appear invisible. That has to change. A serious artist needs more than someone who can write a press release. They need a reputation strategist who understands media, audiences, brands, sponsors, crisis management, data, stakeholder relationships and international markets. They need someone who can distinguish publicity from public relations and publicity from propaganda. Most importantly, they need someone who is not afraid to disagree with them. This is not about importing a foreign model and pretending Ghana has no professional communications expertise of its own. Ghana has talented PR practitioners who understand the local media ecosystem, culture and audience better than any imported playbook ever could. The issue is what the industry rewards and what artist managers demand from those professionals. In mature music markets, artist communications increasingly sits within a broader ecosystem that includes media relations, brand positioning, digital strategy, stakeholder management and crisis communications. The lesson worth borrowing is not a particular Western formula. It is the understanding that reputation management is strategic work, not simply social media combat. PR should build bridges, not deepen the trenches Ghana’s music industry is too small to sustain endless warfare. The same journalist covering Stonebwoy today may cover Shatta Wale tomorrow. The same brand sponsoring Sarkodie may partner with another artist next year. The same promoter working with one camp today may work with its rival tomorrow. Burning relationships for a temporary social media victory is poor business. A professional PR representative should be able to fiercely advocate for an artist without destroying the ecosystem around them. There is nothing wrong with competition, competition can make artists better. Awards should be competitive. Concerts should compete. Songs should compete. Brands should choose who they want to work with. But the professionals behind these artists should not turn competition into permanent hostility. We need to remember that the objective of PR is not to win on Twitter or Facebook. It is to build and protect reputation. And reputation is built slowly, through consistency, credibility, relationships and trust. The CIPR makes a similar point in its definition of PR, describing understanding as a two way process that requires organisations to listen to their publics rather than simply broadcast information. That distinction could transform the way we approach artist communications in Ghana. The industry needs a professional reset I do not think Ghana lacks good publicists. I think good publicists are sometimes being drowned out by bad incentives. We need to redefine what we celebrate. The best PR person should not be the one who insults the rival’s camp most effectively. It should be the one who makes their artist more credible. The best communications team should not necessarily be the one that trends every week. It should be the one that understands when to speak, when to listen, when to clarify, when to apologise and when to remain silent. And the best artist manager should not hire a publicist simply because they have a large following or a reputation for being “savage.” Hire the person who can protect the brand when the room is on fire. Hire the person who can tell you the uncomfortable truth. Hire the person who understands that today’s headline is not more important than tomorrow’s reputation. That is the reset Ghana’s creative industry needs. We need to stop confusing aggression with advocacy, virality with effectiveness and propaganda with PR. Because ultimately, public relations is not about making an artist look perfect. It is about making the artist believable. And in an industry increasingly crowded with noise, credibility may be the most valuable publicity money cannot buy. About the Author Amelley Djosu is a marketing communications strategist, creative entrepreneur and journalist with expertise across media, entertainment, brand communications and the creative economy. She writes and comments on the intersection of culture, creativity and commerce, with a particular interest in the systems, strategies and professional practices shaping Ghana’s evolving creative industry. Through her work, she brings a practical, balanced perspective to conversations around music business, talent management, public relations, branding and the wider creative economy.

items.title: Última hora de la entrada de inmigrantes a Ceuta, en directo | El Gobierno anuncia un mando único para gestionar la crisis de Ceuta
items.description: El ministro de Economía, Carlos Cuerpo, ha anunciado que el Gobierno declarará mañana martes la “situación de interés para la seguridad nacional” en Ceuta y constituirá un mando único para gestionar de forma “rápida y eficiente” la situación en la ciudad. El órgano estará dirigido por el ministro de Administraciones Públicas y Memoria Democrática, Ángel Víctor Torres, e integrado por un “comité especializado” en el que estarán el presidente ceutí, Juan Jesús Vivas, el delegado del Gobierno en la ciudad, los ministros implicados, representantes del CNI, y será asesorado por el Departamento de Seguridad Nacional. Cuerpo ha anunciado también una “ampliación extraordinaria” del plan de crecimiento económico de Ceuta. A las 8.30 de este martes está convocado el Consejo de Seguridad Nacional, 26 días después de que unas 80.000 personas cruzaran de forma irregular la frontera de Marruecos a Ceuta los días 30 y 31 de julio. En el plano sanitario, el Ministerio de Sanidad y las comunidades autónomas enviarán a Ceuta 45.000 vacunas para prevenir que se propaguen enfermedades infecciosas entre los inmigrantes que llegaron a finales de julio, así como para proteger a la población local.
