items.title: 2027: Nigeria needs faithful leaders, not Muslim or Christian president — Idowu-Fearon
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo KADUNA — Former Secretary-General of the Anglican Communion Worldwide and founder of the Kaduna Centre for the Study of Christian-Muslim Relations, Bishop Josiah Idowu-Fearon, has urged Nigerians to look beyond religious identity when choosing political leaders in the 2027 general elections. Idowu-Fearon, who is also a former Chairman of the Kaduna State Peace Commission, said Nigeria needed a president who genuinely practised the values of his or her faith, rather than one chosen solely on the basis of religious identity. The bishop spoke on Monday in Kaduna while responding to questions on the economy, religious leadership, politics, insecurity and the 2027 elections. “Nigeria, honestly, this country does not need a Muslim or a Christian president. What we need is a president who is Christian or Muslim. There is a difference,” he said. He said the same principle should apply to governors, senators, ministers and other public office holders, arguing that neither Christianity nor Islam encouraged corruption, dishonesty, tribalism or exploitation. According to him, Nigerians should assess political leaders based on their character, performance, integrity and commitment to the common good rather than their religious identity. Don’t be too close to politicians Idowu-Fearon also cautioned religious leaders against becoming excessively close to politicians, warning that dependence on political figures for financial and other benefits could undermine their moral authority. “As religious leaders, whether an Imam or a priest, a Sheikh or a Bishop, whatever — when you begin to frequent politicians, you get corrupted,” he said. He added: “If I give you money, if I make sure that you are very comfortable, you cannot challenge me. You’d rather become economical with the truth, and that is the problem we are facing.” The bishop stressed that the problem was not peculiar to Muslim clerics, noting that Christian religious leaders could also be compromised by excessive political influence. He said religious leaders had a responsibility to represent their communities before God and uphold the principles of their respective faiths in society. Government must acknowledge hardship On the economy, Idowu-Fearon challenged the Federal Government to acknowledge the hardship confronting millions of Nigerians rather than appearing to deny its severity. He said his regular interactions with ordinary people during visits to churches and communities in Kaduna had exposed him to the impact of rising living costs. “To say people are not suffering as a result of what is going on in our country, I think we are being economical with the truth,” he said. According to him, some families could barely afford basic necessities, while some worshippers were struggling to pay transportation fares to attend church services. “You can see suffering. There is no doubt about that. A good number of people just have one meal a day. They can hardly even have a balanced meal,” he said. The bishop questioned the impact of increased government revenues and allocations to states and local governments, asking where the benefits were being felt by ordinary Nigerians. “I also heard the Minister of Finance talking about trillions coming in, trillions going to the state governors, going to the local government chairmen. And I ask, where is the money? Where is this money?” he asked. He cited rising prices of household items as evidence of the pressure on citizens, recalling that a bathroom soap holder that previously cost about N500 was recently quoted to him at N5,000. “Something that we were paying about 500 Naira for, 5,000! Tomatoes, anything you ask, they tell you thousand, thousand. What do we do?” he asked. He also expressed concern over electricity supply, saying his residence had been without public power supply for several days. Rather than deny the hardship, Idowu-Fearon urged the government to clearly explain its economic policies and measures being taken to ease the burden on Nigerians. “Instead of denying, government should say, ‘We are aware. This is what we are doing, this is what we are doing,’” he said. Kaduna Muslim-Christian arrangement Commenting on Governor Uba Sani’s decision to return Kaduna to a Muslim-Christian political arrangement, Idowu-Fearon said the decision reflected the state’s political and religious realities. He noted that Kaduna had previously operated arrangements in which Muslims and Christians occupied the two top executive positions before the administration of former Governor Nasir El-Rufai adopted a Muslim-Muslim ticket. “However, the political terrain in Kaduna supports what Governor Uba Sani has done. The terrain supports it,” he said. The bishop, whose doctoral research focused extensively on Kaduna State’s religious and social composition, expressed hope that the arrangement would promote greater cooperation among the three senatorial zones. “We should pray that this decision will bring better understanding and cooperation between the three senatorial zones in Kaduna State,” he said. Religious leaders should not dictate votes Ahead of the 2027 elections, Idowu-Fearon urged religious and traditional leaders to educate voters without dictating whom they should support. “I don’t subscribe to a traditional ruler, a Bishop, or whoever telling members what to do,” he said. He called for debates and greater public scrutiny of candidates, urging religious leaders to help Nigerians understand the responsibilities of elected officials and assess their performance. “We should have debates. We should encourage debates!” he said. He described it as wrong for religious leaders to use their authority to direct their followers to vote for particular candidates. “It is wrong… for any religious leader to say, you should vote for this person,” he said. He added that Nigerians would ultimately be accountable for how they exercised their franchise. “For this 2027 election, with all we’re going through, every vote, God is going to ask you, ‘How did you use your franchise?’” Insecurity On insecurity, the former Peace Commission chairman acknowledged improvements in some parts of Kaduna State, particularly Birnin Gwari, but urged security authorities not to relent. “The government is trying, but… they should not relent. They should keep the pressure on those who are committed to creating problems,” he said. He specifically commended the improvement in the security situation in Birnin Gwari. “Birnin Gwari today, as far as I’m concerned, is a part of the state we can flag, because things have really gone down a bit,” he said. Peace Commission ended constitutionally Idowu-Fearon also clarified the circumstances surrounding the end of the Kaduna State Peace Commission, which he previously chaired. He said the commission’s enabling law provided for a five-year tenure and that its mandate had already extended beyond that period. “We had stayed for more than five years. I think we were driving into our sixth or seventh year,” he said. He explained that the decision followed discussions with the Kaduna State Government and was not the result of any disagreement between the commission and the administration. “So, it wasn’t by fiat. We had discussions,” he said. According to him, the focus was expected to move from conflict resolution towards conflict prevention, while discussions were continuing on possible collaboration between the Kaduna Centre and the government. “There was no bad blood, no bad feeling. It was a constitutional matter,” he said. Population figures should not become religious contest The bishop also cautioned Nigerians against turning Christian and Muslim population figures into a political competition. “As a student of Christian-Muslim relations, I object to that,” he said. He urged both faith communities to focus instead on their shared values and responsibilities to society. Idowu-Fearon said religious institutions had an important role to play in shaping the values of young Nigerians, stressing that life should not be reduced to the pursuit of money and material possessions. “Life is not just money, it’s not just money. It’s not material possession,” he said. He urged Christian and Muslim leaders to work together to teach young people to respect human dignity irrespective of religious affiliation. “Don’t look at me as a Kaduna Christian; look at me as a human being,” he said, adding that both the Bible and the Quran affirmed the dignity of humanity. He said his Kaduna Centre was already using interfaith initiatives, including scriptural reasoning, to encourage Muslims and Christians to explore their shared values. “We have a lot in common. We are created by the same God, we are endowed by the same God,” he said. He urged Nigerians to judge political leaders by their character and performance rather than their faith. “You have honour, you have dignity, and I should see it in you,” Idowu-Fearon said. “When you look at me, don’t say ‘this is an infidel,’ don’t say ‘this is a Christian,’ say this is a human being with honour from God… and with dignity.” The post 2027: Nigeria needs faithful leaders, not Muslim or Christian president — Idowu-Fearon appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Des sites d’orpaillage clandestins démantelés, 40 personnes interpellées
items.description: La gendarmerie sénégalaise a démantelé plusieurs sites d’orpaillage clandestins dans la localité de Mouran, commune de Missira Sirimana. L’opération, menée le 22 août 2026 par le point d’appui du Groupe d’Action Rapide de Surveillance et d’Intervention numéro 2 (GARSI 2) de Saeinsoutou, a conduit à l’interpellation de 40 personnes et à la saisie de plusieurs équipements utilisés pour l’exploitation minière illégale. L’information a été rendue publique ce lundi 24 août 2026 par la Gendarmerie nationale du Sénégal. Dans le cadre de ses opérations de sécurisation et de lutte contre l’exploitation illégale des ressources minières, le point d’appui du Groupe d’Action Rapide de Surveillance et d’Intervention numéro 2 (GARSI 2), basé à Saeinsoutou, a mené une opération contre des sites d’orpaillage clandestins dans la zone de Mouran, relevant de la commune de Missira Sirimana. L’intervention, effectuée le 22 août dernier, a permis aux forces de sécurité d’interpeller 40 personnes. Parmi elles figurent 11 ressortissants burkinabè, 9 Guinéens, 16 Maliens et 4 Sénégalais. Les gendarmes ont également mis la main sur un important lot de matériels présumés utilisés dans les activités d’orpaillage illégal. La saisie comprend notamment 20 motos, 14 motopompes, 8 panneaux solaires, 7 groupes électrogènes ainsi que 5 marteaux-piqueurs. Cette opération s’inscrit dans les actions menées par la Gendarmerie nationale pour lutter contre l’exploitation clandestine des ressources minières et renforcer la sécurisation des zones d’orpaillage. À travers cette intervention, les autorités sénégalaises entendent maintenir la pression sur les activités minières illicites, dont les conséquences peuvent être importantes sur la sécurité, l’environnement et la gestion des ressources naturelles. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Des sites d’orpaillage clandestins démantelés, 40 personnes interpellées est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Cause of Warri-Itakpe train derailment yet to be ascertained — NRC
items.description: …Records four deaths, 64 injured in preliminary report By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Nigerian Railway Corporation (NRC) has released its preliminary report on the June 8, 2026, Warri-Itakpe Train Service (WITS) derailment, confirming that four people, comprising three adults and a child, died in the incident, while 64 others were injured. The corporation, however, said the definitive cause of the derailment had yet to be established. The incident occurred at about 4:17 p.m. near the Goodluck Jonathan Railway Station in Owa-Oyibu, Delta State. According to the preliminary report, the train departed Itakpe at noon with 482 persons on board, comprising 442 passengers and 40 operational personnel, when five coaches, one locomotive and a power car derailed at kilometre 177. “Three of the coaches and the power car overturned, while other rolling stock derailed but remained upright,” the NRC stated. NRC Managing Director, Kayode Opeifa, who disclosed the report on Monday, said emergency response was activated immediately, with support from the Delta State Government, Nigeria Police Force, Federal Road Safety Corps, National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), local authorities and medical teams. He said all passengers were evacuated within two hours of the incident. Of the 64 injured persons, 28 passengers were treated and discharged at the Railway Hospital, Owa-Oyibu, while another 36 were taken to general hospitals in Owa-Oyibu, Owa-Alero and the Central Hospital, Agbor. “Most of those admitted were discharged within 72 hours. Three persons, including one NRC personnel who required surgical intervention, remain under specialist medical care and two subsequently had surgical procedures carried out,” the report stated. The NRC also clarified that an initial report of five fatalities was revised to four after verification with the Delta State medical team. The corporation expressed condolences to the families of the deceased. Preliminary findings According to the report, the NRC constituted an internal investigation team that conducted site inspections, collected evidence, reviewed operational records, examined the locomotives and rolling stock and interviewed crew members, staff and emergency responders. The team identified a possible sudden development of a bogie or wheel defect while the train was in motion as a potential primary factor in the derailment. “Based on preliminary observations, the team cited a possible cause, indicating the possible sudden development of a bogie/wheel defect while en route. This observation is being investigated further as a potential primary factor in the derailment,” the report stated. It explained that such a defect could have resulted in abnormal wheel-rail interaction, excessive impact loading and loss of running stability. The NRC added that the possible manner of brake application might also have contributed to the severity of the incident. “These remain working hypotheses. The definitive cause or causes of the accident will be determined through comprehensive analysis and will be set out in the final report,” it said. Unlike the derailments recorded on the same route on November 1 and November 8, 2025, the NRC said its inquiry team found no evidence of track vandalism. “Site examination by the inquiry team observed that the points were intact and that no evidence of track vandalism was found,” it stated. The Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) has also commenced an independent investigation into the incident. The NRC said it was cooperating fully with the NSIB investigation and would be guided by its findings and recommendations. Recommendations The NRC said its internal review produced six key recommendations, including strengthening rolling stock and infrastructure management through comprehensive inspections, audits and timely replacement of defective components. It also recommended reviewing and strengthening operational safety procedures through updated standard operating procedures and stricter enforcement of safety compliance. Other recommendations include improving emergency preparedness and response through regular drills and enhanced inter-agency coordination; strengthening human capacity through continuous training and competency assessments; and providing sustainable funding for railway modernisation, infrastructure development and asset optimisation. The corporation also recommended strengthening passenger and staff welfare protection by reviewing insurance and compensation frameworks. “The corporation’s priority is to strengthen railway safety, improve operational resilience and restore public confidence in rail transportation,” the NRC said. Status of operations The corporation confirmed that the affected track had been fully recovered and restored, while the locomotives had been recovered and were undergoing reconditioning. It said resumption of train services would depend on the completion of a detailed track and equipment safety audit. The NRC explained that the delay in releasing the preliminary report was necessary to ensure that every relative of those involved was duly informed through its structured medical and victim support procedures. The post Cause of Warri-Itakpe train derailment yet to be ascertained — NRC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Médina Baye, la merveille qui rayonne depuis Kaolack
items.description: À Kaolack, le nom de Médina Baye dépasse depuis longtemps les limites d’une simple cité religieuse. Il évoque une histoire, une école de pensée, une communauté et un rayonnement qui s’étend bien au-delà du Sénégal. Née autour de Cheikh Al Islam El Hadji Ibrahima Niass, Baye Niass, à la fin des années 1920 et au début des années 1930, la cité est devenue l’un des principaux foyers de la Fayda Tijaniyya et un point de convergence pour des fidèles venus de nombreux pays. L’histoire commence avec Baye Niass, né en 1900 à Taïba Niassène. Les sources ne s’accordent pas toutes sur l’année exacte de fondation de Médina Baye. Certaines évoquent 1929, d’autres 1930 ou 1931. La période généralement retenue se situe donc entre 1929 et 1931, avec 1930 comme date fréquemment citée. Ce qui demeure établi, c’est que Baye Niass fait progressivement de ce site le centre de son œuvre et que la cité se développe autour de son enseignement religieux et spirituel. Avant même l’essor de Médina Baye, l’enseignement de Baye Niass rayonne déjà dans son environnement. À Kossi notamment, il dispense un enseignement religieux et organise des rassemblements qui participent à la diffusion de son message. Cette dynamique contribue ensuite à l’émergence de Médina Baye comme nouveau centre de la Fayda Tijaniyya. À mesure que les disciples affluent, Médina Baye prend forme. La prière, l’étude du Coran, l’enseignement des sciences islamiques et la vie communautaire structurent progressivement la nouvelle cité. Son nom, inspiré de Médine, la ville du Prophète Muhammad (PSL), traduit la forte dimension spirituelle que Baye Niass entend donner à cette implantation. Mais l’histoire de Médina Baye ne s’arrête pas à Kaolack. L’enseignement de Baye Niass franchit progressivement les frontières sénégalaises. Le Nigéria occupe une place particulière dans cette expansion. Les déplacements de Baye Niass, ses relations avec plusieurs responsables religieux et politiques, ainsi que l’engagement de ses disciples contribuent à l’enracinement de la Fayda dans plusieurs régions du pays. Le rayonnement s’étend ensuite à d’autres espaces d’Afrique de l’Ouest, puis à des communautés établies notamment en Europe et en Amérique du Nord. Cette dimension internationale doit beaucoup aux générations de disciples et d’érudits qui ont poursuivi l’œuvre du fondateur. Après la disparition de Baye Niass en 1975, ses fils, ses proches et ses disciples assurent la continuité de son enseignement. Parmi les figures qui ont particulièrement contribué à son rayonnement figure Cheikh Hassan Ali Cissé, plus connu sous le nom d’Imam Assane Cissé. Par son enseignement, ses déplacements et son ouverture sur le monde, Imam Assane Cissé participe largement à la diffusion de l’héritage de Baye Niass, notamment auprès de communautés musulmanes aux États-Unis et dans d’autres régions du monde. Son action contribue à inscrire durablement la Fayda Tijaniyya dans une dynamique internationale. Aujourd’hui, cette continuité est incarnée par Cheikh Mouhamadoul Mahi Ibrahima Niass, cinquième khalife général de Médina Baye. Son magistère accorde une place importante à la paix, au dialogue et à la médiation. En 2022, il s’est notamment illustré par une mission de médiation au Darfour, au Soudan, où il a participé à des démarches visant à rapprocher les parties engagées dans un conflit et à favoriser le retour au calme. Mais c’est lors du Mawlid que le rayonnement de la cité prend toute sa dimension. Chaque année, Kaolack accueille des fidèles venus du Sénégal, de plusieurs pays d’Afrique et de la diaspora. Les rues se remplissent, les maisons ouvrent leurs portes, les programmes religieux se multiplient et les différentes communautés se retrouvent autour de la célébration de la naissance du Prophète Muhammad (PSL). Dans cette foule, le caractère international de Médina Baye devient particulièrement visible. Des fidèles venus du Nigéria et d’autres pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest côtoient des Sénégalais et des membres de communautés établies notamment en Europe et en Amérique du Nord. Pendant quelques jours, les distances semblent s’effacer au profit d’une même tradition spirituelle et d’une même ferveur. Près d’un siècle après ses premières années d’existence, Médina Baye présente un visage profondément transformé. Pourtant, l’essentiel demeure : l’enseignement, la transmission et la fidélité à l’héritage de Baye Niass. Son influence ne se mesure donc pas seulement à l’affluence du Mawlid. Elle se lit aussi dans les écoles, les érudits, les familles et les communautés qui, génération après génération, ont porté cet héritage bien au-delà de Kaolack. Baye Niass avait fait émerger un foyer spirituel. Ses héritiers et ses disciples l’ont inscrit dans la durée et lui ont donné une dimension internationale. Médina Baye est ainsi devenue une merveille singulière : une cité née à Kaolack dont le nom, l’enseignement et le rayonnement continuent de voyager bien au-delà des frontières du Sénégal. Papa Abdoulaye Sy

items.title: Amélioration génétique bovine : la Guinée prépare l’arrivée de 5 000 bovins du Brésil
items.description: La Guinée prévoit d’introduire progressivement 5 000 bovins de races améliorées en provenance du Brésil dans le cadre du Programme national d’amélioration génétique bovine, Horizon 2026-2035. Un premier lot de 2 500 animaux est prévu dans cette opération présentée ce lundi à Conakry, par le ministère de l’Élevage. La rencontre a réuni le ministre de l’Élevage, Alpha Bacar Barry, des représentants brésiliens, un ancien ministre sénégalais de l’Agriculture et de l’Élevage, des représentants d’une quinzaine de banques guinéennes ainsi que des compagnies d’assurances. Selon les statistiques agricoles citées par Alpha Bacar Barry, la Guinée compte environ 8 millions de bovins, mais importe encore 60 % de la viande et 80 % du lait consommés dans le pays. Le ministre estime que ces données traduisent la nécessité de moderniser la production locale et d’améliorer les performances du cheptel. « Il faut qu’on sorte de l’élevage de prestige, il faut qu’on sorte de l’élevage traditionnel, il faut qu’on aille vers un élevage moderne et intensif », a-t-il déclaré. Les 5 000 bovins annoncés doivent être introduits en deux phases. Les premiers animaux seront sélectionnés au Brésil, selon leurs caractéristiques génétiques, avant leur passage dans des centres de quarantaine où ils feront l’objet de contrôles sanitaires et de traitements prophylactiques. Ils seront ensuite acheminés vers la Guinée. Fabio Costa, représentant d’AgroBetel, partenaire brésilien de l’opération, a indiqué que les animaux sélectionnés sont issus de races adaptées aux conditions tropicales. Il a toutefois insisté sur l’importance de l’alimentation, estimant que la génétique ne peut produire les résultats attendus sans une alimentation adaptée et disponible. À leur arrivée, les bovins doivent être confiés à des entrepreneurs et éleveurs guinéens, avec un accompagnement dans les domaines vétérinaire, zootechnique, financier et assurantiel. Le dispositif prévoit notamment que certains bénéficiaires puissent rembourser l’appui reçu en argent ou en lait. La reproduction des animaux doit également permettre d’étendre progressivement les races améliorées à d’autres exploitations. Le ministère prévoit par ailleurs de poursuivre l’amélioration génétique du cheptel à travers l’insémination artificielle et le transfert d’embryons. Le programme doit également favoriser le développement d’activités liées à l’élevage, notamment la production d’aliments pour bétail, les équipements, les services vétérinaires, la collecte et la transformation du lait ainsi que la transformation de la viande. Le financement constitue un autre volet important du projet. Pour Diallo Mamadou Lamarana, représentant d’Access Bank Guinée, l’élevage demeure encore un secteur peu financé par les banques. Il estime que la structuration de cette initiative pourrait permettre aux établissements financiers de mieux évaluer les risques et de proposer des mécanismes de financement adaptés aux besoins des éleveurs. L’ancien ministre sénégalais de l’Agriculture et de l’Élevage, qui accompagne le projet à travers son cabinet MD Advisory, intervient notamment dans la structuration financière de l’opération. Il a évoqué des mécanismes tels que les lettres de crédit, les crédits documentaires et les traites avalisées pour faciliter l’importation des premiers bovins. Selon ses estimations, la Guinée aurait besoin de produire entre 800 millions et un milliard de litres de lait par an pour atteindre son autosuffisance, sur la base d’une consommation moyenne d’environ 50 litres par habitant et par an. Il estime également que le développement de la filière pourrait générer des emplois dans plusieurs secteurs liés à l’élevage. Pour le ministère de l’Élevage, le programme Horizon 2026-2035 s’inscrit dans la vision Simandou 2040 et vise à réduire progressivement la dépendance de la Guinée aux importations de viande et de lait. La première phase de 2 500 bovins doit servir de point de départ, avant l’introduction du second lot portant le total à 5 000 animaux.

items.title: Bourd à Paris : la ferveur tidiane au cœur de la diaspora
items.description: À Paris, cette année encore, la communauté tidiane de France, l’une des plus dynamiques de la diaspora, s’est mobilisée pendant les dix jours du Bourd pour vibrer au rythme de la ferveur spirituelle du Mawloudou Nabi, à l’initiative de la Zawiya Seydina Cheikh de Paris. Des centaines de fidèles issus des différentes dahiras d’Île-de-France se sont rassemblés chaque jour depuis l’ouverture du Bourd à Tivaouane, marquant le début des célébrations de la naissance du Sceau des Prophètes, Seydina Mouhamed (SAW). En France, comme partout ailleurs en Europe, l’héritage spirituel de Tivaouane demeure un rendez-vous à ne pas manquer. Cette dynamique est portée par les guides religieux. Serigne Abdou Aziz Sy Al Amine avait notamment appelé les responsables à faire de l’unité leur maître-mot, à organiser collectivement les Burds et le Gamou en s’inspirant de Tivaouane, et à œuvrer à l’acquisition d’une Zawiya à Paris. Quinze ans après les premiers Burds collectifs, cette recommandation se poursuit avec un objectif : offrir aux générations présentes et futures un lieu durable de prière, de transmission et de rassemblement. Ousmane Noël MBAYE, à Paris (France)

items.title: La Russie pointée du doigt après la découverte d'un drone à Leipzig : «à Kiev, on célèbre le succès de l'opération», rapporte le renseignement russe
items.description: « Sans meme attendre les resultats preliminaires de l'enquete, les hommes politiques allemands de tous rangs, suivis par les medias europeens, ont rendu un verdict sans appel : "la main de Moscou" avait atteint une infrastructure aeroportuaire allemande essentielle », a souligne dans un communique paru ce 24 août le Service russe de renseignement exterieur (SVR), qui evoque des « informations recues » par ses soins. En toile de fond : la decouverte d'un drone a proximite d'un avion de transport ukrainien, dans la nuit du 4 au 5 août, a l'aeroport allemand de Leipzig/Halle. Une infrastructure presentee dans les medias comme un « hub logistique cle pour l'Otan ». L'avion sans pilote avait ete – comme le raconte Euronews – decouvert « quatre heures apres la collision » par un « chauffeur de bus aeroportuaire » qui lui a « marche dessus ». « Les explosifs se retrouveraient apparemment a une certaine distance », a precise le media europeen. Des que la decouverte a ete annoncee dans la presse, l'ambassadeur de Kiev en Allemagne n'avait pas perdu de temps pour accuser la Russie d'etre derriere cette presomption d'attaque de drones perpetree directement sur le sol d'un pays membre de l'OTAN. « Qui d'autre cela pourrait etre a part la Russie ? » avait declare celui dont le pays a deja tente d'entraîner ses soutiens occidentaux dans son conflit avec la Russie. Cette promptitude ukrainienne a blâmer la Russie n'est pas sans rappeler celle qu'avait eue le bureau de Zelensky dans la foulee du sabotage de Nord Stream en septembre 2022. Un episode de terrorisme international qu'a d'ailleurs rappele un SVR resigne : « pouvait-on s'attendre a un autre developpement d'evenements ? », peut-on lire dans son communique. Soutien a Kiev : les Europeens « stimules » par cet episode Pour leur part, les autorites allemandes, notamment par la voix du ministre de l'Interieur, Alexander Dobrindt, ont estime que l'incident securitaire relevait d'« une nouvelle dimension de menace » pesant sur l'Allemagne, sans toutefois pointer un coupable du doigt. Une prudence, alors que la justice allemande semble resserrer l'etau autour de l'Ukraine dans l'affaire Nord Stream, ce qui a deplu a certaines voix dans les medias. D'autres personnalites, dans les medias allemands, n'avaient pas pris autant de pincettes, certaines allant jusqu'a appeler a une « riposte » contre la Russie. « Kiev se felicite vivement de l'impact mediatique et politique de l'incident », a insiste le SVR, precisant que cet incident aurait « stimule » les Europeens, « les incitant a vider leurs depots militaires pour assurer la survie du regime de Kiev ». Pour autant, le SVR semble garder foi en ses homologues allemands et « le professionnalisme qui les caracterise ». D'apres le communique, « la presence d'une "piste ukrainienne" est serieusement envisagee en coulisses » par les enqueteurs allemands. « La question demeure », a poursuivi le SVR, avant de conclure : « les autorites allemandes auront-elles le courage politique de reconnaître publiquement des conclusions impartiales ? »

items.title: Ogun 2027: APC reaffirms Yayi’s candidacy, dismisses Hunye
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress (APC) has reaffirmed Senator Adeola Solomon Olamilekan, popularly known as “Yayi,” as its authentic governorship candidate for the 2027 Ogun State election, dismissing the candidacy of Mr Abayomi Hunye as unauthorized. The party also said Hunye remained suspended from its membership. In a statement issued on Monday, APC National Secretary, Senator Ajibola Basiru, described Hunye as an “impostor” and said his claim to the party’s governorship ticket was unauthorized. According to Basiru, Hunye was suspended from the party on April 7, 2026, following a petition from his ward, Tube Ward, in Ipokia Local Government Area of Ogun State. The party said the suspension was based on a decision by the ward executives, which was subsequently ratified by the Ipokia Local Government Area and approved by the Ogun State Working Committee. Basiru said the suspension followed allegations of “engaging in activities injurious to the image of the Party” and “deliberate actions aimed at causing disaffection and division among loyal members.” He added that, as a result of the suspension, Hunye lacked the standing to represent the APC in any capacity. The APC reaffirmed that Senator Olamilekan remained its duly nominated candidate following the party’s governorship primary election, with Balogun Kudirat Abiodun as his running mate. The party said the particulars of Olamilekan and Abiodun had been submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in accordance with the Electoral Act 2026 and the commission’s guidelines. It said INEC had issued acknowledgement slips confirming the submission of their particulars as the party’s candidates for the election scheduled for January 2027. Documents attached to the statement, including INEC’s temporary acknowledgement of submission, showed that the candidates’ profiles were submitted on Friday, August 7, 2026. The APC cautioned individuals and organisations against conducting political transactions with Hunye, saying the party would not be responsible for any financial loss, legal disputes or criminal liability arising from such dealings. The party also disclosed that its legal team had been directed to initiate contempt proceedings and file a formal complaint with security agencies over what it described as “gross misrepresentation and impersonation.” The APC further cautioned media organisations against providing a platform for Hunye, saying such action could be interpreted as complicity in what it described as a fraudulent act. It urged its supporters in Ogun State to remain calm and law-abiding and to ignore what it described as provocations aimed at disrupting peace in the state. “For clarification and official updates,” the party said, members of the public should contact the APC National Secretariat through the Office of the National Secretary. items.title: Cameroun : l’ancien international Oliver Kahn annoncé à Douala
items.description: © America TV L'ancien capitaine de la sélection nationale allemande et ancien PDG du FC Bayern Munich ouvrira EXPSummit 2026 les 1er et 2 octobre prochains à Douala dans le cadre de sa première keynote en Afrique. La deuxième édition de l'EXPSummit se tiendra dans la capitale économique du Cameroun dès le 1 er octobre 2026. Oliver Kahn prendra part à des échanges d'expériences et de perspectives en qualité de keynote speaker. L'ancien capitaine d'Allemagne sera aux côtés de dirigeants, cadres et des experts pour échanger autour du thème : « Façonner l'avenir grâce aux innovations pertinentes ». Les travaux s'articuleront autour de trois forums recélant trois enjeux. Le premier, Leadership forum, sera consacré aux enjeux des dirigeants, à la cohésion d'équipe et aux leviers humains de la croissance. Prévu pour le 1er octobre en matinée, ce forum vise à montrer comment le leadership, la confiance et la collaboration permettent de construire des équipes hautement performantes. Des intervenants à ce forum seront des chefs d'entreprise reconnus pour leur capacité à transformer une ambition en résultats concrets, conduire leur organisation à travers des crises, instaurer durablement un véritable esprit d'équipe. Le second forum, l'Expert forum, sera dédié aux innovations multisectorielles et aux solutions mobiles qui transforment les modèles économiques. Il sera question d'explorer la manière dont les solutions mobiles transforment la finance, les ressources humaines, la mobilité, le marketing et le diversement. Prévu le 1er octobre en après-midi, il regroupera des dirigeants et experts issus des secteurs de la finance, des ressources humaines, de la mobilité, du marketing ou du divertissement. Le troisième forum, Emerging Experts Forum, sera tourné vers la nouvelle génération de talents, les nouveaux formats de contenu et les expertises émergentes. Prévu le 02 octobre, il poursuit l'objectif de renforcer la crédibilité, développer la visibilité et construire une influence durable grâce à des contenus stratégiques et de qualité. Il sera animé par des jeunes cadres, entrepreneurs, créateurs et professionnels émergents issus de la création de contenu, des métiers créatifs, de l'industrie et des professions libérales. Oliver Kahn, Keynote Speaker EXPSummit 2026 EXPSummit 2026 déroule le tapis rouge à Oliver Kahn, figure emblématique du football mondial qui a réussi la transition du sport de haut niveau au leadership d'entreprise. Ancien gardien et capitaine du FC Bayern Munich et de l'équipe nationale d'Allemagne, il cumule entre 1988 et 2008, huit titres de champion d'Allemagne et six Coupes d'Allemagne. Il est aussi vainqueur de la Ligue des champions et de la Coupe intercontinentale en 2001. Finaliste de la Coupe du monde 2002, il est le premier gardien élu meilleur joueur d'une coupe du monde. Consultant sportif, conférencier, il va briller par ses analyses et sa participation à des programmes de formation à Harvard et Stanford entre 2008 et 2020. Dès janvier 2020, il sera membre du directoire du FC Bayern, puis PDG du même club. Oliver Kahn est entrepreneur, investisseur et philanthrope depuis 2008. Il investit dans le sport, les médias et le management en Europe. Il va partager son expérience au cours de l’événement. Rencontre professionnelle réunissant des dirigeants, experts et talents émergents, Expérience Summit explore les innovations les plus pertinentes. Le but étant de les mettre au service de la croissance et de la performance des organisations. L'événement est organisé par le Réseau de solutions (RDS) regroupant des agences et des cabinets-conseils disposant d'une expertise multidisciplinaire et intercontinentale dans le domaine du marketing, de la technologie, de l'événementiel et de la performance commerciale. Cet article Cameroun : l'ancien international Oliver Kahn annoncé à Douala est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Crisis rocks Oyo NDC as chairman, secretary clash
items.description: By Adeola Badru A fresh crisis has reportedly erupted within the Oyo State chapter of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), following a breakdown in relations between the State Chairman, Princess Oyeronke Akinlolu, and the State Secretary, Comrade Okunade Aderoju. The disagreement is said to be centred on allegations of misconduct, lack of internal consultation and unilateral decision-making by the state chairman. The development has reportedly heightened tension within the party’s state leadership, with Aderoju accusing the chairman of allegedly engaging in inter-party activities without the approval of relevant party organs and running the chapter as a “one-man administration”. Aderoju, in a statement on Monday, alleged that several important decisions affecting the party had been taken without adequate consultation with the State Executive Committee, describing the development as a violation of the principles of collective responsibility and internal democracy. “Several important decisions affecting the party have been taken without adequate consultation with the State Executive Committee, and this undermines the collective responsibility and democratic principles upon which party leadership should operate,” he said. The state secretary further alleged that Akinlolu had engaged in activities involving other political interests without obtaining the necessary approval or consulting the relevant organs of the national leadership of the NDC. “The State Chairman has engaged in activities involving other political interests without obtaining the necessary approval or consultation with the relevant organs of the National NDC,” he alleged. Aderoju said the party belonged to its members and should not be operated at the discretion of any individual. “The party belongs to its members. It cannot be operated solely at the discretion of one individual, regardless of the position that individual occupies,” he said. He stressed the need for all party officials to adhere to the NDC constitution and established rules. “The NDC is a political organisation governed by its constitution, rules and collective decisions. “No individual, regardless of position, should run the party as a personal organisation or take decisions that bind the party without proper consultation,” he added. The secretary also raised concerns over what he described as “gross misconduct”, insisting that elected and appointed party officials must remain accountable to the appropriate organs of the organisation. “Party officials must be accountable to the appropriate organs of the party and must operate within the limits of their offices. No office gives anyone the authority to act outside the constitution or established rules of the organisation,” he said. Aderoju said the alleged actions had raised concerns among party stakeholders, particularly over the direction and administration of the Oyo State chapter. “What we are concerned about is not an individual or personal ambition. Our concern is the integrity of the party, the sanctity of its constitution and the collective interest of our members,” he said. He said the disagreement had widened in recent days, with both sides allegedly taking divergent positions on the administration and direction of the state chapter. Calling for urgent intervention, Aderoju appealed to the appropriate national organs of the party to intervene before the situation escalated. “We are calling for urgent intervention by the appropriate national organs of the party. The situation must not be allowed to escalate to a point where it will further divide our members or damage the confidence people have in the party,” he said. He said the objective of the intervention was to restore unity, discipline and confidence within the state chapter. “Our intention is to see unity restored, discipline maintained and confidence rebuilt among party members. This is bigger than any individual,” Aderoju stated. The state secretary maintained that his position was not motivated by personal interest or political ambition, but by what he described as a commitment to protecting the party and its members. “My position is not motivated by personal interest or ambition. It is about protecting the integrity of the NDC, its constitution and the collective interests of our members in Oyo State,” he said. He appealed to party members, Local Government chairmen, State Executive Committee members and other stakeholders to remain calm while the appropriate organs work towards resolving the disagreement. “I appeal to all our party members, Local Government Chairmen, members of the State Executive Committee and other stakeholders to remain calm and committed to the NDC. We should allow the appropriate organs of the party to address these issues and find a lasting solution,” he said. Aderoju urged members to remain focused on the party’s principles and collective objectives, stressing that the constitution should guide all activities. “We must not lose sight of why the NDC exists. Our collective interests must always come before individual interests, and the constitution of the party must remain our guide,” he said. The post Crisis rocks Oyo NDC as chairman, secretary clash appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Canada seeks foreign nurses, pharmacists, social workers for employment
items.description: Canada is seeking skilled professionals from around the world to join its workforce as the country looks to address labour shortages across several key and emerging industries. The Canadian government said international professionals with the right skills and experience can access various immigration pathways to build careers and settle in communities across the country. The recruitment drive covers several sectors, including science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), healthcare, skilled trades, defence and cybersecurity, critical minerals, and education. Canada is also particularly seeking skilled healthcare and social service professionals to help address shortages within its healthcare system. Professionals being sought include nurse practitioners, dentists, pharmacists, psychologists and social workers, among others. According to the government, qualified professionals with the required training, credentials and work experience can explore available immigration pathways to work and build a future in Canada. The country is also highlighting the benefits available to international talent, including career opportunities with a wide range of employers and access to services designed to help newcomers settle. Canada said immigrants can also benefit from safe and stable communities, quality education and training opportunities, as well as a multicultural environment that embraces diversity in people, ideas and languages. French-speaking newcomers can also access dedicated community services designed to support their settlement and integration. The recruitment initiative comes as Canada continues to attract skilled workers to strengthen its labour force and address shortages in sectors considered important to the country’s economy. For professionals considering a move to Canada, the government encourages applicants to review the eligibility requirements of relevant immigration programmes and ensure they have the necessary qualifications, credentials and experience before applying. Healthcare and social service professionals in particular are being encouraged to explore immigration options as Canada seeks to strengthen its workforce and provide essential services to its growing population. items.title: Wills to 2027 Candidates: No Niger Delta cleanup, no vote
items.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa Veteran governance and environmental rights advocate, Iniruo Wills, has urged presidential and governorship candidates in the 2027 general elections to present clear and concrete plans for addressing decades of environmental pollution in the Niger Delta or risk losing the region’s votes. Wills, a former two-time Bayelsa State Commissioner for Information and Environment, made the call in an interview with Vanguard in Yenagoa. He spoke against the backdrop of the unveiling of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate Peter Obi’s campaign agenda, which focuses on security, economic recovery, healthcare, education and national unity, but contains no explicit reference to a comprehensive cleanup of the Niger Delta. Wills described the omission as a major oversight that could affect the candidate’s support in the region if not addressed. “There is obviously no Niger Deltan in PO’s strategy team,” he said. “Any presidential candidate that has no explicit concrete plan for the region, including a Niger Delta-wide environmental cleanup, should be rejected by the region.” Wills, who has consistently advocated against environmental degradation in the Niger Delta, urged those close to Obi to draw his attention to the concerns of the region. “He cannot tell us he has been touring the country for six to eight years now and does not know the cardinal demands of some of the regions. No more papaye in our elections,” he said, using the local expression to criticise what he described as superficial campaign promises. The environmental rights advocate, who had previously criticised Niger Delta governors, ministers and senators over their handling of environmental pollution in the region, called on political candidates to embark on genuine listening campaigns and community-based consultations before finalising their manifestoes. “Principal candidates, presidential and gubernatorial, should learn to do a listening campaign, or real and felt people or community-based consultations, before they roll out their manifestoes on a roadshow,” he said. Wills extended the call to all major political parties, including the All Progressives Congress (APC), African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). He urged the parties to present specific and credible plans for cleaning up polluted communities in the Niger Delta if they wanted the support of voters in the region. “Only such candidates should be voted for in 2027. No Niger Delta Cleanup, no vote for you or your party,” Wills declared. He described the position as a “Civil Society Campaign Challenge for 2027”, with the slogan, “No Cleanup, No Vote.” Wills also called on traditional rulers, civil society organisations and community leaders to mobilise voters across the nine oil-producing states to support only candidates who make credible commitments to addressing environmental degradation in the region. He described decades of oil pollution, gas flaring and ecological degradation in the Niger Delta as “ecocide”, arguing that the scale and duration of the environmental damage required stronger political accountability from successive administrations. Wills cited the Bayelsa State Oil and Environmental Commission report, which characterised the environmental condition in the state as “environmental genocide”. “It’s in our hands. Let’s bargain with our votes and stop complaining afterwards,” he added. The post Wills to 2027 Candidates: No Niger Delta cleanup, no vote appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: A Freedom 250 Event That Actually Worked
items.description: An interest in the thrills of car racing is not what drove me to spend my Sunday afternoon at the Freedom 250 Grand Prix, the latest of the spectacles that Donald Trump has presided over during the United States’ big birthday celebrations all summer. I was there yesterday because I was worried about art. The event involved 25 cars zipping around a number of D.C.’s museums and historic buildings at worryingly high speeds— 147 times . Preservationists and conservators had raised concerns ahead of the contest, leading me to imagine creaking sculptures and rattling ceramics, all because the president wanted a race around the National Mall. Seeing the National Gallery of Art’s huge black Alexander Calder sculpture outside, surrounded by wood boards as if the poor thing were hunkering down for war, didn’t help. But it turns out that playing art patrol is rather difficult at an IndyCar race, especially when you find yourself crammed into a sweaty crowd as blurs of color whiz by. This proximity to the action means you are a participant in a much more visceral way than at many other sporting events: You can feel the vibrations in your toes. Somewhere among the vroom s, I realized that this was not like the other Freedom 250 productions I had attended, like the Great American State Fair with its drab triumphal arch and the Freedom Trucks with their selective history. Instead, in some moments, the Grand Prix was … fun? The good vibes began when I spotted the driver Sting Ray Robb’s maintenance truck, decorated with the ridiculously wholesome image of seven puppies climbing on his race car. He immediately gained a fan in me, though he crashed early on. The course, with its many bumps, was tricky for drivers, and just more than half of them even finished. Kyle Kirkwood, another American, won. Many might be tempted to slot the IndyCar race next to other Trumpian events that have disrupted life in the nation’s capital. More than that, the race could easily serve as another example of how little an administration that has pressured museums and diluted historic-preservation laws cares for the nation’s cultural heritage. These interpretations aren’t overblown. Earlier this year, the Grand Prix unveiled (and later walked back) a disturbing T-shirt that featured a white-clad figure and read: One Nation One Race . In and around the city yesterday, the traffic was a pain for locals, the nearest airport had to stop flights for three hours, and the noise—including multiple deafening flyovers—was nothing short of a public nuisance. For those without tickets, access to the Mall was closed off. Madhan Subramanian, who lives by the course, told me he was “just a little annoyed by everything.” He thought it was a cool event, but “it was harder to get groceries and just do our normal thing.” The worries about vibrations and damage to artifacts were legitimate, too. In the middle of the race, I put my hand on the boarded-up geometric I. M. Pei skylights outside the National Gallery and found them shaking like a cellphone on vibrate. (Not great!) A man yelled to me over the thunderous cars, “Are we okay?” I replied, in earnest, “I’m not sure.” (So far, there have been no reports of damaged art.) Reckless is one word for what unfolded in the capital yesterday. But one person’s reckless is another’s exciting . And the Freedom 250 Grand Prix certainly had oomph to it. Trump did a lap of the track at the beginning of the race to the sound of mixed cheers and boos, and although I noticed Trump gear— Trump 2028 hats, for example—for sale outside the race perimeter, inside many fans had opted for checkers and race jerseys. In other words, this didn’t feel like another Freedom 250 event that was more about Trump than about America. Race-car driving occupies its own indomitable universe of fandom, kitsch, design, and hype. Ultimately, a race is a race, and many in the crowd appeared to be there simply for the sport. Keith Cole, a former amateur racer and F1 fan, was among them. A car race in downtown Washington seemed like a once-in-a-lifetime thing, so he came to D.C. with a friend despite some low-grade partisan energy they didn’t care for. “We don’t see a lot of people like us here,” Cole, who is Black, told me, noting some MAGA-hat sightings, too. “I understand how they want to use it to politicize it, but this is sports. You gotta, kind of, take it out of it.” Most of the time, the National Mall is a reflective space flanked by quiet, regal buildings that command a certain respect. Yesterday, though, America’s “front yard” felt more like a backyard. IndyCar fans played cornhole and giant Connect Four on the grass, which was dotted with lemonade stands and picnic tables. In one moment, I was surrounded by beer-drinking racing fanatics; in the next, I was engulfed in the smell of gasoline and the sound of revving engines; minutes later, after a short stroll, I was standing in the National Gallery in front of a Georgia O’Keeffe. Inside one of the galleries, I found Carol Madden—a native of Indianapolis, IndyCar’s namesake and the site of its premier event, the 500—seeking a break from the heat near some Renaissance-era earthenware. “The Indy 500 is Christmas for my family. We don’t come home for Christmas and Easter—we all come home for the race,” she told me. This was her 55th race, which she attended with her whole family, she said, getting teary-eyed. Nearby, Diana Vinson, as much a race-car fan as a museum lover, was immersed in a photograph on the wall. She didn’t see her appreciation for the two things as entirely separate. Both art and racing are all about precision; they’re about tiny decisions—in brushstrokes or tire pressure—that add up. “You have to understand your mediums,” she told me. The museum was making the most of any connection it could find with the event, which forced it to partially close for the race; the portion of it that remained open was accessible only to IndyCar ticket holders. (The National Gallery has been notably savvy about garnering attention of late, as evidenced by its viral videos of a Gen Z–whispering senior curator who called that Renaissance earthenware “bussin’.”) Outside, signs promised “iconic art (and air-conditioning).” Staff members had set up a tent where they sold T-shirts featuring a portrait of George Souders, who won the Indy 500 in 1927, from the museum’s collection. Earlier, out on the Mall, I had spoken with Bill Sherman, a fan of “anything that makes noise and goes fast,” who told me he thinks people are drawn to car racing because they can see themselves in it. “I’ve driven these roads hundreds of times,” he said. “It’s one of the few sports that you can look at and say, I can go out and do that every day on the Beltway .” Though that would certainly spice up your commute, you shouldn’t. Just like you shouldn’t send thousands of pounds of metal flying around historic sites. But watching cars hurtling past the National Archives, barreling toward the Air and Space Museum, with the U.S. Capitol looming in the distance, you might just convince yourself otherwise.

items.title: INEC opens accreditation for September 2026 rerun elections
items.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has opened its online accreditation portal for media organisations seeking to cover the September 2026 rerun elections in selected constituencies across the country. INEC announced that the accreditation process commenced on Monday, August 24, 2026, through its INEC Media Accreditation Portal (IMAP). The affected constituencies include Sakwa State Constituency in Bauchi State, Udu State Constituency in Delta State and Dawakin Kudu State Constituency in Kano State. Media organisations interested in deploying journalists and other relevant personnel to cover the elections are required to apply through the portal. The commission said the portal would close at midnight on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, stressing that there would be no extension of the deadline. INEC said accreditation would be conducted strictly online, adding that no manual applications would be entertained. It also warned that late submissions would not be accepted, as the portal would automatically shut down at the expiration of the deadline. According to the commission, only credible and duly registered media organisations would be considered for accreditation. “Media organisations are advised to complete their applications and nominations well before the deadline,” INEC said. The commission urged interested media organisations to ensure that all required information and documents were properly uploaded before the portal closes. For enquiries and technical assistance with the accreditation portal, INEC provided the following contact numbers: 07088844564 and 08032861058. INEC said the accreditation exercise was part of arrangements for media coverage of the forthcoming rerun elections. The post INEC opens accreditation for September 2026 rerun elections appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Why flooding is ravaging Nigeria — Sliding Towers
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu A Nigerian building construction and consultancy company, Sliding Towers Global Ltd, has attributed the recurring flooding in parts of the country to poor adherence to building regulations and urban planning standards. The company, in a statement issued in Awka, said flooding had become a recurring feature of Nigeria’s rainy season, stressing that although rainfall often triggers flooding, the severity of the resulting damage is frequently linked to decisions made long before the rains begin. It noted that the 2026 flood season was particularly significant, citing the Nigeria Hydrological Services Agency’s annual flood outlook, which identified 14,118 communities across 266 Local Government Areas in 33 states and the Federal Capital Territory as high-risk flood areas. “Every rainy season, the images return. Roads disappear beneath water. Cars stall. Homes are submerged. Businesses shut their doors and entire neighbourhoods become temporarily inaccessible. “Yet rainfall alone does not explain why one storm passes relatively unnoticed while another becomes a disaster. The answer is often on the ground,” the company said. Sliding Towers identified the construction of buildings over natural waterways, disappearance of wetlands, excessive paving of compounds, blocked or undersized drainage channels and poor consideration of natural water flow in the design and development of buildings as factors worsening flooding. “Flooding, therefore, is not simply a drainage problem; it is also a question of planning, architecture and the way we build our cities. And that means flood resilience should begin much earlier than the emergency response. “It should begin on the drawing board,” it said. According to the company, architects and developers should consider the topography of a site, existing drainage paths, soil conditions and potential flood exposure before determining where and how buildings should be constructed. It said relatively simple measures could significantly reduce flood risks in vulnerable areas, including raising finished floor levels, protecting entrances from direct runoff and positioning electrical equipment, generators and other critical infrastructure above anticipated flood levels. “Water needs somewhere to go. When almost every surface becomes impermeable, rainfall that would once have soaked gradually into the ground is rapidly converted into runoff and directed towards already stressed public drains,” it said. The company advocated the use of permeable paving, planted areas, rain gardens, landscaped depressions and rainwater harvesting as part of building and urban designs. It added that roof water could be harvested and reused, while site levels could be designed to slow down and safely direct excess runoff. “Flood resilience does not mean putting every Nigerian building on stilts. It means designing each building according to the realities of its site. “The principle is more important than any particular solution. Buildings should be designed with water in mind; not designed first and defended from water afterwards,” it said. Sliding Towers also cautioned against viewing improved drainage solely as the construction of more concrete channels, noting that no drainage network would perform effectively if every roof, driveway, road and paved compound discharged water into it simultaneously. It stressed that flood resilience must be addressed at four interconnected levels — the building, street, neighbourhood and city. “A well-designed house is still vulnerable when the street outside is under water. A carefully drained office building cannot function when the surrounding road network becomes inaccessible. “Flood resilience must therefore operate at four scales, namely, the building, the street, the neighbourhood and the city,” the company said. It called for the protection of natural drainage corridors and wetlands, warning against treating such areas as vacant land available for development. According to the company, parks and other open spaces can also serve dual purposes by providing recreational areas during normal weather while temporarily accommodating stormwater during periods of heavy rainfall. “The goal should not simply be to move water away as quickly as possible, but to understand where it naturally wants to go, slow it where possible, store it where appropriate and ensure that buildings and communities can withstand the remaining risk,” Sliding Towers said. The post Why flooding is ravaging Nigeria — Sliding Towers appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Eliminatoires de la CAN 2027 : Le Maroc face au Gabon et au Lesotho en septembre
items.description: Le Maroc entamera les éliminatoires de la CAN 2027 le 25 septembre 2026 face au Gabon à Rabat, avant de se déplacer en Afrique du Sud pour affronter le Lesotho le 29 du même mois à Bloemfontein. items.title: Gourma/Tourisme : La Fédération régionale des acteurs du tourisme officiellement portée sur les fonts baptismaux à Fada N’Gourma
items.description: BURKINA-GOURMA-TOURISME-BUREAU-INSTALLATION Gourma/Tourisme : La Fédération régionale des acteurs du tourisme officiellement portée sur les fonts baptismaux à Fada N’Gourma Fada N’Gourma, 24 août 2026 (AIB)-Les acteurs du tourisme des régions du Goulmou, de la Sirba et de la Tapoa ont installé, ce lundi 24 août 2026 à Fada N’Gourma, le bureau de la Fédération régionale des acteurs du tourisme (FRAT) de l’Est. La cérémonie a été présidée par le Haut-commissaire de la province du Gourma, Silas Nacanabo, représentant le Gouverneur de la région du Goulmou. Cette nouvelle organisation faîtière regroupe l'ensemble des professionnels et acteurs du secteur touristique issus des régions du Goulmou, de la Sirba et de la Tapoa. Elle vise à offrir un cadre d'échange et de concertation unifié pour promouvoir la destination Est et soutenir la relance du secteur. A l'issue des travaux de concertation, Mathieu Ouoba a été porté à la tête de cette faîtière régionale en qualité de président du bureau exécutif. « C'est une mission que nous devons mener main dans la main avec tous les acteurs pour atteindre nos objectifs. Notre ambition est que les régions du Goulmou, de la Sirba et de la Tapoa soient vraiment une fierté et que les choses se passent comme il se doit a déclaré le nouveau président de la Fédération régionale des acteurs du tourisme (FRAT) de l’Est, Mathieu Ouoba. Pour lui, en matière de tourisme, nous allons développer des initiatives et sensibiliser les gens pour que le secteur voie le jour et se développe dans notre région. Le Directeur du développement de l'industrie touristique, Kadré Sawadogo, s'est félicité de la naissance de cette organisation, concrétisée avec l'accompagnement technique de la direction régionale en charge du tourisme. « Cette fédération régionale répond à la nécessité de trouver un cadre commun qui permettra aux acteurs du tourisme de s'exprimer et de réfléchir à des actions constructives afin d'apporter leur contribution aux actions de l'administration nationale du tourisme», a expliqué Camarade Sawadogo. Selon le président de la FRAT-Est, face aux nombreux défis du secteur dans notre contexte actuel, il était temps pour les acteurs de se ressouder afin que leur voix puisse porter. Le Directeur du développement de l'industrie touristique a ajouté que la faîtière s'assigne trois missions principales qui sont, assurer la représentation globale des acteurs du secteur, œuvrer aux côtés de l'administration publique à la gouvernance du tourisme et renforcer la cohésion ainsi que la synergie d'action entre tous les acteurs des régions du Goulmou, de la Sirba et de la Tapoa. Le Haut-commissaire de la province du Gourma, Silas Nacanabo, a salué la dynamique engagée par les professionnels du secteur et les a exhortés à faire de cette structure un levier incontournable pour la valorisation du potentiel touristique de la région de l'Est. Agence d’information du Burkina KAC/HB/OO

items.title: 5 newest countries in Africa
items.description: Africa is home to 54 recognised countries, but some of them are considerably younger than others. While many African nations gained independence in the 1950s and 1960s, a handful became independent much later. The continent’s newest country is South Sudan, which gained independence in 2011 after decades of conflict and a referendum on self-determination. Here are the five newest countries in Africa, based on their dates of independence: 1. South Sudan – 2011 South Sudan is the newest country in Africa and the youngest internationally recognised country in the world. It became independent from Sudan on July 9, 2011, following a referendum in which an overwhelming majority of voters backed independence. The country emerged after years of civil war between forces in northern and southern Sudan. Its capital and largest city is Juba. 2. Eritrea – 1993 Eritrea became independent from Ethiopia on May 24, 1993, following a prolonged armed struggle. The country had been federated with Ethiopia in 1952 before Ethiopia annexed it in 1962. The subsequent independence war lasted for about three decades. Eritrea’s capital is Asmara, which is known for its distinctive Italian colonial-era architecture. 3. Namibia – 1990 Namibia gained independence from South African rule on March 21, 1990, becoming one of Africa’s newest sovereign states at the time. The country had previously been known as South West Africa and was administered by South Africa for decades. Namibia is located in southwestern Africa and is known for its vast desert landscapes, including the Namib Desert. Its capital is Windhoek. 4. Zimbabwe – 1980 Zimbabwe became an independent nation on April 18, 1980, following years of armed conflict and political negotiations. The country was formerly known as Rhodesia under white minority rule. Independence followed the Lancaster House Agreement, which paved the way for democratic elections. Harare became the capital of the newly independent country. 5. Djibouti – 1977 Djibouti became independent from France on June 27, 1977, making it the fifth-newest country in Africa. The country was previously known as the French Territory of the Afars and Issas. Following a referendum and negotiations with France, Djibouti achieved independence. Located in the Horn of Africa, Djibouti occupies a strategically important position near the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. Its capital, Djibouti City, is also the country’s largest urban centre. items.title: World Cup winners, FIFA legends say Infantino blinded by power
items.description: A group of former international players, including World Cup winners and FIFA legends, called on Monday for immediate change at world soccer’s governing body, saying its leadership under embattled President Gianni Infantino had been blinded by power. Infantino has been under mounting pressure to resign after shelving his now abandoned proposal to create a commercial body for FIFA tournament rights and sell off 20 per cent to private investors. The Swiss has shown no signs of walking away from the position he has held since 2016 despite open opposition from several of FIFA’s own confederations , including UEFA, the AFC and CONCACAF, amid talks of a potential no-confidence vote. “We share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world,” said former players including France’s 1998 men’s World Cup winners Emmanuel Petit, Bixente Lizarazu and Robert Pires as well as American former women’s world champion Briana Scurry and former England international Lucy Bronze. “Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under FIFA’s current leadership. Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football,” the group said. Reuters has contacted FIFA for comment. The group also includes former Peru forward Claudio Pizarro, former Argentina international Juan Sebastian Veron, former Togo captain Emmanuel Adebayor, and FIFA legends Didier Drogba and David James. FIFA legends are former players recognised for their contributions to the sport who help promote football on behalf of the global body, playing in exhibition matches and supporting social and charity projects worldwide. “We call on all stakeholders to step forward and help reshape the future of our sport. There are good people within FIFA who want to rebuild trust, but a new era requires a structural change: a real, direct say for players and fans in how football is run,” the group said. Infantino is up for re-election next year but world soccer’s regional powerhouses are discussing whether to move a vote of no confidence in him ahead of the ballot, senior figures familiar with the discussions told Reuters last week. “Those who step onto the pitch and those who sit in the stands deserve a genuine voice to help reshape football’s future together. For the fans, for the players, and for the good of the game, we will be silent no more,” the players’ group said.
