items.title: Justin Kodua urges delegates to endorse him ahead of October polls
items.description: Incumbent General Secretary of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Justin Frimpong Kodua, has urged delegates to retain him in the party’s October national executive elections, saying his continued leadership will help strengthen the party and position it to return to the Jubilee House in 2029. Mr Kodua made the appeal after filing his nomination to contest the general secretary position at the NPP headquarters on Monday, August 24. Addressing party supporters, Mr Kodua said he was confident in his record and ability to lead the party through its reorganisation following its defeat in the 2024 general election. He said the party entered the 2024 election with the ambition of “breaking the eight” but was unable to retain power. Mr Kodua, however, stressed that despite the defeat, the NPP remained a strong political force. “We all know the party went into a very difficult election in 2024. And because we knew the election was going to be a difficult one, we came out with a mantra termed as breaking the eight. “Though we couldn’t win the elections, the New Patriotic Party continued to remain a strong party,” Mr Kodua said. Party faced turbulence after 2024 defeat According to Mr Kodua, the NPP went through a particularly difficult period in 2025 following its electoral defeat. He said the period was characterised by tension, confusion, acrimony, disagreements, and uncertainty, with some party members becoming concerned about the future of the NPP. “Many of you were very worried, looking at the tension, the confusion, the acrimony, the disturbances, and the uneasiness in our party,” Mr Kodua said. “Many of you felt that 2025 was going to be a very difficult year for the New Patriotic Party. At that point, some of you thought that the party was even going to collapse.” Mr Kodua said the party leadership subsequently took what he described as a bold and unprecedented decision to elect its presidential candidate before conducting the other internal elections. He acknowledged that the decision attracted criticism at the time but maintained that it had ultimately helped restore calm and stability within the party. “But when the party decided to take a bold decision for us to have calmness, to have peace, and to have order in our party, we decided to take a decision that has never been taken before. A very decisive decision, but at that time very unpopular,” he said. Mr Kodua recalled that the decision to elect the flagbearer first was met with criticism from some members of the party. “When we said that in order for the party to have peace and calmness, we needed to start the election with our flagbearer, I remember when we took that decision, many people chastised the general secretary and members of the National Council,” he said. “But I can tell you that today we have been vindicated,” he added. Claims credit for party reorganisation Mr Kodua also highlighted his role in the reorganisation of the party, pointing to the successful completion of internal elections at various levels. He said the NPP had conducted elections at the polling station, electoral area, constituency, and regional levels, describing the process as one of the most peaceful and successful internal election exercises in the party’s history. “By electing our flagbearer first, it has ensured that there is peace in our party. And the person who led us to take that decision is your own general secretary,” Mr Kodua said. He added that his leadership had been instrumental in guiding the party through its reorganisation. “I assure you that as the man who has led the reorganisation of our party through ensuring successful polling station elections, successful electoral area elections, successful constituency elections, and successful regional elections, all of you attest to the fact that we have organised one of the most peaceful and successful internal elections the party has ever had,” he said. According to Mr Kodua, the successful internal elections have helped restore confidence and enthusiasm among party members. “Indeed, as I speak to you today, the New Patriotic Party spirit is back,” he said. Calls for continuity ahead of 2028 Mr Kodua said the NPP’s immediate focus should now be on building a united and effective party ahead of the 2028 general election. He urged delegates to elect executives who would work towards securing victory for the party and ensuring that its flagbearer, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, becomes President of Ghana. “The only thing left is for us to come 3rd of October to elect executives who will work to make sure that His Excellency Dr Mahamudu Bawumia becomes the president of Ghana in 2028,” Mr Kodua said. He further stressed the importance of maintaining a strong working relationship between the General Secretary’s office and that of the party’s flagbearer. “And I can assure you that, indeed, you have a general secretary who works comfortably with the flagbearer,” he said. “You have a general secretary who has a good working relationship with the office of the flagbearer,” Mr Kodua added. He argued that retaining him would help preserve the cordial relationship between the party’s administrative leadership and the office of the flagbearer. “In order for us to continue to ensure that cordiality, there is the non-negotiable need for us to maintain the general secretary of our party,” he said. Predicts endorsement in Kumasi Mr Kodua expressed confidence that delegates would back his bid for another term when the NPP holds its national executive elections in Kumasi on October 3. He said he expected the contest to be less about a competitive election and more about an endorsement of his leadership. His bid for another term comes as the NPP seeks to consolidate its structures and rebuild after losing the 2024 presidential and parliamentary elections. The October elections will determine the team that will lead the party as it prepares for the 2028 general election, with Mr Kodua seeking to retain his position and continue what he describes as the party’s ongoing reorganisation. Mr Kodua is set to face three other contenders: former Subin Member of Parliament Eugene Boakye Antwi, Slyvester Tetteh, and Charles Dwamena.

items.title: Government eases Bawku motorbike restrictions from August 25
items.description: Government has eased restrictions on motorbike riding in Bawku Municipality and its environs in the Upper East Region, allowing both men and women to ride between 6:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. daily. The revised arrangement takes effect on Monday, August 25, following a review by the Minister for the Interior on the advice of the National Security Council and through an Executive Instrument. Under the new directive, residents will be permitted to ride motorbikes during the 12-hour daytime period, representing a relaxation of restrictions that have previously affected motorbike use in the area. The Interior Ministry said the decision was taken as part of measures concerning security and public order in Bawku Municipality and surrounding communities. The revised directive specifically permits both men and women to ride motorbikes from 6:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. every day. The government has, however, maintained restrictions covering the night-time period. The easing of the motorbike restriction does not affect the existing curfew, which remains in force from 10:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. The government has also maintained a total ban on the possession and carrying of arms, ammunition and offensive weapons within Bawku Municipality and its environs. According to the directive, all persons within the affected area are prohibited from carrying arms, ammunition or any offensive weapons. The government warned that anyone found in possession of arms or ammunition would be arrested and prosecuted. The government has also appealed to traditional leaders, community leaders and residents to exercise restraint in responding to the challenges confronting the area. It specifically called on Chiefs, Elders, Opinion Leaders, Youth and the people of Bawku to help promote peace and stability. The government urged residents to use non-violent means to express their concerns and channel their energies towards finding peaceful solutions to the challenges facing the municipality and its surrounding communities.

items.title: Jeffrey Nortey honoured for digital influence at National ICT Week 2026
items.description: Actor, content creator and creative entrepreneur Jeffrey Nortey has been honoured at the National ICT Week 2026 Recognition Awards for his influence and impact in Ghana’s digital and entertainment space. Jeffrey Nortey received the ‘Recognition for Outstanding Influence and Impact in the Digital and Entertainment Space’ award at the National ICT Week 2026 Recognition Awards and Dinner held in Accra on Friday, August 21. The recognition came as part of a week that brought together stakeholders from government, industry, academia, media and the creative sector to examine Ghana’s digital transformation and the opportunities emerging across the country’s technology ecosystem. The award recognised Jeffrey Nortey’s growing use of digital platforms and technology to build a creative brand and connect with audiences. The organisers described his work as an exceptional use of technology to promote and elevate his craft within the creative industry, noting the contribution of his digital platforms to the growth and visibility of his work. However, Jeffrey Nortey’s involvement in the National ICT Week went beyond receiving an award. Before the recognition dinner, he was selected as one of the creative voices to contribute to the programme’s dialogue on day three, where he participated in a dedicated “Creators’ Exchange” designed to test policy and institutional perspectives against the everyday realities of people building careers and businesses online. The session brought Nortey and fellow creator Hilda Ama Braso into direct conversation with experts and institutional representatives on issues affecting Ghana’s digital creative economy. The session objective was specifically to examine areas including account security, impersonation, privacy, intellectual property, online abuse, brand partnerships, AI generated content and platform accountability. For Jeffrey Nortey, the discussion offered an opportunity to bring the creator’s perspective into conversations that are often dominated by policy, technology and institutional language. His contribution focused on the practical realities of building a public identity and commercial brand through social media. Among the issues highlighted were account hacking, impersonation and fake profiles, unauthorised reposting and commercial exploitation of skits, ownership of characters and creative concepts, cyberbullying, reputational attacks and harmful audience behaviour. He also raised questions around the responsibilities of creators when using comedy and social commentary to address sensitive issues, as well as the potentially serious impact of platform suspensions and demonetisation on creators whose livelihoods depend heavily on digital platforms. The format of the session allowed creators to put direct questions to representatives from institutions dealing with cybersecurity, telecommunications, law and digital regulation. Among the issues proposed for discussion were what immediate support is available when a creator’s account is hacked or cloned, how creators can protect original characters, scripts and catchphrases, and what recourse exists when global platforms suspend or demonetise an account. The discussion also placed particular attention on intellectual property and the growing challenge of protecting creative work in an increasingly digital environment. For creators such as Nortey, whose characters, scripts, catchphrases and skits form a significant part of their commercial identity, questions around ownership and unauthorised exploitation are increasingly tied to both creative and financial sustainability. The broader programme reflected NITA’s role in Ghana’s digital ecosystem. NITA describes its mandate as creating an enabling environment for the effective deployment and use of ICT through sound policies and regulatory frameworks. National ICT Week 2026 was held from August 17 to 20 at the Cedi Conference Centre, University of Ghana, Legon, under the theme ‘Innovation at Scale: Creating Opportunities Across Ghana’s Digital Ecosystem.’ The programme provided a platform for conversations around Ghana’s digital transformation, including technology, cybersecurity, digital finance and the broader opportunities created by innovation. Jeffrey Nortey’s presence at the event was therefore significant beyond the award itself. His participation reflected the increasingly important place of creators within Ghana’s digital economy, where entertainment, technology, intellectual property, advertising and entrepreneurship increasingly intersect. His recognition also comes at a period of growing expansion in his creative career. In June, Nortey staged the third edition of 3 Faces of Jeffrey Nortey at the National Theatre, combining film, theatre and live character performance in a sold-out production that further demonstrated how a digital character and online audience can be translated into a broader live entertainment experience. From comedy skits and character creation to film, theatre, brand partnerships and now conversations around digital policy, Jeffrey Nortey’s career illustrates the changing nature of the modern Ghanaian creative entrepreneur. The National ICT Week honour consequently recognises more than his visibility online. It acknowledges the influence that creators can wield when digital platforms become tools for storytelling, enterprise and cultural expression. As Ghana continues to build a more secure, innovative and inclusive digital ecosystem, voices such as Nortey’s will remain important in ensuring that policy conversations reflect not only the technology being developed, but also the people whose livelihoods and identities increasingly depend on it. items.title: Édouard Mendy élu meilleur gardien d’Arabie Saoudite
items.description: La saison 2025-2026 d’Édouard Mendy a été célébrée avec le trophée de meilleur gardien d’Arabie Saoudite. Le gardien de but sénégalais a remporté le « Gant d’Or », qui récompense le meilleur gardien de but de la saison, devant le Marocain Yassine Bounou. Déjà une distinction pour Édouard Mendy. Le gardien de but sénégalais a été élu meilleur portier de la Saudi Pro League lors de la saison 2025-2026. Le gardien des Lions a reçu sa récompense à l’issue de la victoire d’Al-Ahly sur Abha (4-0), comptant pour la troisième journée du championnat. La saison dernière, le gardien international sénégalais a été exceptionnel dans les buts d’Al-Ahli. Il a gardé ses cages inviolées à 14 reprises. Les statistiques impressionnantes du double champion d’Afrique ne se sont pas arrêtées là. Édouard Mendy a aussi réalisé 46 arrêts et stoppé 3 penaltys. En championnat, le gardien de 34 ans a encaissé 18 buts, ce qui fait un pourcentage de 0,69 but encaissé par match. Grâce à cette excellente saison, l’ancien portier de Chelsea a aussi aidé Al-Ahly à remporter à nouveau la Ligue des champions asiatique, la deuxième successive. Il a gardé cette belle forme lors du Mondial 2026 en réalisant de belles prestations malgré les défaites contre la France (3-1) et la Norvège (3-2). Durant ce match face à la Norvège, il avait dû céder sa place à cause d’une blessure. Cette blessure l’avait écarté pour le reste de la compétition. Face à l’Irak (5-0) ou contre la Belgique, le champion d’Asie avait été suppléé par Mory Diaw. Ce samedi, face à Abha de son compatriote Abdou Diallo, Mendy effectuait son grand retour dans les buts d’Al-Ahly, après avoir manqué la première journée. Il s’est distingué en enrayant plusieurs occasions de but dont une d’Abdou Diallo. Avec une note de 8,3 sur 10, Édouard Mendy a la troisième meilleure note de la rencontre derrière son coéquipier Ivan Toney auteur d’un triplé et Trincao qui a inscrit un but. Julien Mbesse SÈNE

items.title: Four labourers killed by unknown assailants in Balochistan's Pishin district
items.description: QUETTA: Four labourers working on an under-construction road were killed by unidentified armed men near the Saranan area of Balochistan’s Pishin district on Tuesday. Officials said the incident took place in the Sulemanzai area along the Quetta-Chaman Highway. Balochistan Chief Minister’s aide for political and media affairs Shahid Rind confirmed the incident. “The labourers were working on an under-construction road in the area when armed men targeted them,” Rind said, adding that one labourer sustained injuries and was taken to the district hospital along with the bodies. Police and security forces rushed to the site and started an investigation. “Armed men arrived at the site on motorcycles and opened fire on the labourers,” a senior police officer posted in the area said on condition of anonymity. He added that the four labourers were killed on the spot after sustaining multiple bullet wounds. Sources said the victims were from Punjab and had come to the area in search of work. The incident was the second such attack in the area in the past three days. On Friday, armed men blew up a police station in Saranan town in the presence of hundreds of people, planting explosives after taking control of the facility. According to official sources, armed men entered the town’s bazaar and surrounded the local police station. They entered the building, took police personnel hostage and ransacked official records. The attackers later planted explosives at different points inside the police station before bringing the police personnel out of the building and detonating the explosives. Officials said no one was killed or injured, although the police station was badly damaged. Police said on Sunday that five bodies, including those of four men who had reportedly been shot dead, were recovered from different parts of Balochistan, including Chaman, Mastung and Sohbatpur. Earlier this month, eight people were killed in separate incidents across Balochistan, including a passenger bus driver shot dead in Kachhi and two people gunned down in Khuzdar, police said. According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies’ (PICSS) monthly security assessment released on July 31, the security situation deteriorated most significantly in Balochistan in the country last month. The overall death toll increased by 241pc in Balochistan, from 109 in June to 372 in July, the report said. Security personnel deaths in Balochistan increased from six in June to 62 in July, representing a rise of 933pc. Terrorist deaths rose from 75 to 238, while civilian deaths increased by 93pc, from 28 to 54. Eighteen members of peace committees were also killed in the province.

items.title: «Nous n’avons pas commencé cette guerre, mais nous ne permettrons pas qu’elle se termine aux conditions de l’agresseur», affirme le ministère iranien des Affaires étrangères
items.description: L'Iran a reaffirme qu'il n'accepterait pas une fin du conflit dictee par ses adversaires. Le porte-parole du ministere iranien des Affaires etrangeres, Esmaïl Baghaï, a assure ce 24 août que Teheran ne cederait pas sur la defense de sa souverainete et de son integrite territoriale. « Nous n'avons certainement pas commence la guerre, mais nous ne permettrons pas que sa fin soit determinee aux conditions de l'agresseur », a-t-il declare. Baghaï a egalement estime que ceux que Teheran considere comme les initiateurs du conflit devaient assumer la responsabilite de leurs actes. « L'agresseur doit repondre de ses actes », a-t-il insiste. La diplomatie iranienne a parallelement adresse un avertissement aux pays mettant leurs infrastructures a la disposition des forces americaines. Selon Baghaï, lorsqu'un territoire est utilise pour mener des operations contre l'Iran, Teheran se reserve le droit de repondre contre « la source ou le point de depart » de l'action hostile. Le message concerne notamment la Bulgarie, ou etaient stationnes des avions ravitailleurs americains. Plusieurs de ces appareils auraient depuis quitte le pays. Teheran a presente leur deploiement comme une forme de soutien aux operations militaires menees par les etats-Unis et Israel contre l'Iran. Cette fermete est egalement affichee par le commandement militaire iranien. Le general Amir Hatami a insiste sur la capacite du pays a poursuivre sa defense sur le long terme et sur le role de son industrie nationale de defense. Il a averti que l'Iran ne devait pas etre considere comme un terrain d'experimentation pour des « aventures militaires ». Ormuz au centre des echanges regionaux Dans le meme temps, Teheran maintient ses consultations avec plusieurs acteurs regionaux. Le ministre omanais des Affaires etrangeres, Badr ben Hamad al-Busaidi, doit se rendre dans la capitale iranienne pour discuter notamment de la securite du detroit d'Ormuz et des routes maritimes. L'Iran a egalement confirme la visite du chef de l'armee pakistanaise, Asim Munir, alors que Teheran et Islamabad cherchent a renforcer leurs relations. La diplomatie iranienne a precise que les visites pakistanaise et omanaise etaient distinctes. Le detroit d'Ormuz demeure l'un des principaux foyers de tension du conflit. Le trafic maritime y a fortement diminue ces derniers jours, alors que cette voie reste essentielle au commerce mondial des hydrocarbures. Teheran a par ailleurs rejete les affirmations americaines faisant etat d'une circulation normale dans le detroit, les qualifiant de guerre de l'information. Washington intensifie la pression economique Le conflit avait connu une tentative d'arret des hostilites en juin avant la reprise des frappes americaines en juillet, Washington invoquant alors un differend autour des engagements lies au detroit d'Ormuz. L'administration americaine entend desormais accentuer la pression economique sur l'Iran. Le secretaire americain au Tresor Scott Bessent a annonce le 23 août l'entree des etats-Unis dans ce qu'il presente comme la « phase finale » du conflit. Il a promis une offensive financiere d'une ampleur sans precedent. Il a qualifie cette nouvelle etape de « jour J economique ». Teheran a conteste cette presentation. Le vice-ministre iranien des Affaires etrangeres Kazem Gharibabadi a pointe ce qu'il considere comme une contradiction dans le discours americain : Washington affirme avoir considerablement reduit le potentiel militaire iranien et affaibli son programme nucleaire, tout en estimant necessaire de mobiliser des moyens economiques exceptionnels contre le pays. Gharibabadi a ainsi demande si cette nouvelle offensive constituait reellement une victoire ou plutot « un amer aveu d'echec ». Face a l'intensification de la pression americaine, Teheran maintient sa position : aucune fin de guerre imposee par ses adversaires, defense de son territoire face aux infrastructures utilisees contre lui et poursuite des contacts regionaux autour d'Ormuz. La nouvelle offensive financiere annoncee par Washington ouvre ainsi un nouveau volet du bras de fer, sans modifier pour l'heure la ligne affichee par les autorites iraniennes.

items.title: Minority challenges Gyamfi to substantiate extortion allegations against Afenyo-Markin
items.description: The Minority in Parliament has challenged Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) Chief Executive Officer, Sammy Gyamfi, to substantiate allegations of extortion made against Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin. The Caucus says the allegations will not distract it from its push for a parliamentary inquiry into what it describes as a US$1.7 billion loss associated with the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP). The Minority maintains that Parliament has several constitutional and procedural mechanisms available to scrutinise the circumstances surrounding the reported loss. Speaking after a Minority Caucus meeting in Parliament on Monday, August 24, Old Tafo MP and Member of Parliament’s Economy Committee, Vincent Ekow Assafuah, said the Caucus would proceed with its chosen strategy despite calls for the matter to be referred to the Public Accounts Committee. “Nobody teaches the Minority as to how it should go about its work. The tools that are available to Parliament are well placed within our hands to use any of the tools that we so deem fit to use,” he said. Mr Assafuah said although the Public Accounts Committee was an available option, the Minority also had the constitutional authority to seek the establishment of an ad hoc committee. “If somebody wants to use the Public Accounts Committee, the person can go ahead to do so. But can the person also tell us that based on Article 103 of the 1992 Constitution and Articles 204, 212, 213, 262, and 263, the Minority is not well placed to come by way of a motion?” he asked. He said the Caucus had submitted a motion to the Speaker of Parliament seeking consideration within the week. According to him, the proposed ad hoc committee would provide Parliament with an avenue to examine the circumstances surrounding the reported loss. “It is an ad hoc motion, an ad hoc committee that is going to help the Minority to be able to unravel the circumstances by which this loss came about,” he said. “And so that is our strategy. We will not bend the rules or we will not bend our strategy for anybody’s convenience.” Minority defends choice of parliamentary procedure Mr Assafuah maintained that Article 103 of the 1992 Constitution gives Parliament the power to establish committees to investigate and inquire into matters relating to ministries, departments and agencies. He also cited several provisions of Parliament’s Standing Orders which, he said, provide a basis for establishing an ad hoc committee and empowering it to invite persons who may assist with an inquiry. “Our Orders are also well placed — Orders 212, 204, 213, 262 and 263 — [and] allow Parliament to establish an ad hoc committee,” he said. He added that such a committee could invite individuals with relevant information to appear before it as part of the inquiry. The Minority’s position comes amid an escalating public dispute between Mr Gyamfi and Mr Afenyo-Markin over the GoldBod and the reported financial losses associated with the DGPP. The Caucus has accused the GoldBod CEO of attempting to divert attention from questions surrounding the programme and has challenged him to provide evidence to support his allegations against the Minority Leader. Mr Assafuah urged stakeholders to focus on the substance of the proposed parliamentary inquiry rather than the particular procedure being advocated by different parties. “Let’s get to the substance of the matter,” he said.

items.title: OSP acknowledges three petitions linked to Afenyo-Markin-Gyamfi dispute
items.description: The Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) has received three petitions concerning extortion allegations made by Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) Chief Executive Officer, Sammy Gyamfi, against Minority Leader in Parliament, Alexander Afenyo-Markin. The OSP said one of the petitions was jointly submitted by two individuals, while two separate petitions were filed by other persons, all in relation to the allegations. In a statement issued on Monday, August 24, the OSP said it had taken note of the public allegations of extortion and related conduct made by Mr Gyamfi against Mr Afenyo-Markin. The office subsequently confirmed that it had received three petitions seeking its attention on the matter. “The OSP also acknowledges a joint petition submitted by two persons, as well as two separate petitions submitted by other persons, in relation to the allegations,” it said. The OSP said receipt of the petitions did not amount to a determination of the truth or otherwise of the allegations. It explained that it would first assess the matter to establish whether the allegations fall within its statutory mandate and whether there are grounds for further investigative action. “Given the nature of the allegations, the OSP will assess the case and determine whether it falls within its statutory mandate and whether further investigative action is warranted,” the office said. READ ALSO: OSP to assess extortion allegations involving Sammy Gyamfi and Afenyo-Markin The development comes amid an escalating public dispute between Mr Gyamfi and Mr Afenyo-Markin over the Minority’s concerns about the financial performance of GoldBod and the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme. Mr Afenyo-Markin has denied the allegations against him and has indicated that he is considering his legal options.

items.title: Iran faces ‘greatest financial offensive ever’, says US treasury secretary
items.description: The US treasury secretary has threated Iran with “the single greatest financial offensive ever”, claiming the US-Israel war with Iran was “entering its endgame”. Scott Bessent said the US would sever all economic ties with the country in “an economic D-Day” and that any nation partnering with Iran financially would also be isolated. Bessent’s threat to the Iranian regime follows several U-turns and extended deadlines from US President Donald Trump’s administration on previous threats. Iran dismissed Bessent’s comments and said it would shut down all oil exports from the region “if the war continues”, according to news agency Reuters. The Iranian regime has also issued a new warning to shipping not to pass through the Strait of Hormuz without its permission, the agency reported. One fifth of the world’s oil and gas usually passes through strait, a waterway south of Iran, but the flow has been effectively blocked by the country since the conflict began at the end of February. Bessent made the comments in an opinion piece for the Financial Times. He did not detail what the economic pressure on Iran would involve, but he is expected to do so in a press conference in the US at 13:00 local time (18:00 BST) on Monday. “The world should understand that our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains the tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone,” he wrote in the piece. The US has made several threats to Iran over the course of its war with the country, including Trump saying in April that “a whole civilisation will die tonight” unless Iran agreed a deal to end the war and unblock the Strait of Hormuz. The US eventually climbed down from that position after mediator Pakistan intervened and called for more diplomacy. The economic impact of the Iran war is being felt in the US and across the world. Higher oil prices have fuelled concerns over the cost of living, with petrol and diesel prices much higher than they were a year ago. In the US, gasoline prices have surpassed $4 a gallon and affordability is among the top concerns of American voters ahead of the mid-term elections in November. Last week, Bessent announced the US government would intervene in the bond markets and buy back more government debt in a bid to boost demand for bonds and lower borrowing rates. But the impact of the annoucenment was short-lived, with long-term borrowing costs bouncing back up a day later. The Iranian regime already faces tough economic sanctions from the US. Former US president Barrack Obama and several US allies had agreed a deal with the country in 2015 which lifted many sanctions in return for Iran agreeing to limit its nuclear programme. However, Trump pulled out of that deal in 2018, calling it “defective at its core, and reimposed all US sanctions on Iran. During Joe Biden’s term as US president, he made some attempts to reinstate the Obama-era deal, but this did not happen. In April this year, the Trump administration launched a wave of sanctions on foreign banks and firms doing business with Tehran after it became clear its military operations had not caused Iran’s regime to surrender.

items.title: Amansie West Assembly inaugurates road safety committee to curb crashes
items.description: The Amansie West District Assembly in the Ashanti Region has inaugurated a nine-member District Road Safety Committee to intensify public education and sensitisation on road safety and help reduce road crashes in the district. The committee, made up of representatives from key institutions and stakeholders, is expected to engage road users and other relevant groups on the causes of road accidents and measures to prevent avoidable crashes. Its membership comprises the District Coordinating Director, traditional leaders, the Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) Commander, the Ghana National Fire Service, the District Medical Director, a representative of the National Ambulance Service, the Ghana Education Service, the District Engineer and the Information Services Department. The District Coordinating Director and Chairman of the committee, Mr Thomas Kwame Okrah, speaking at the ceremony, said the committee had been tasked with undertaking sustained sensitisation programmes for drivers, motor riders, passengers, spare parts dealers and other road users. He said the initiative is aimed at promoting responsible road use and ensuring that road users understand the consequences of reckless and unsafe driving. Mr Okrah called for the cooperation of individuals, transport operators, traditional authorities and other stakeholders to support efforts to reduce road crashes in the district. He noted that road accidents continued to have serious social and economic consequences, including loss of lives, injuries, destruction of property and financial burdens on families and communities. The committee Chairman expressed particular concern about the conduct of some motor riders and urged them to exercise greater caution and discipline while using the roads. According to him, records available to the Assembly indicated that motor riders are involved in a significant number of road crashes recorded in the district, making it necessary to intensify direct engagement with them. Mr Okrah said the committee would, therefore, organise targeted sensitisation programmes for motor riders and other road users to promote compliance with road traffic regulations and responsible use of the roads. He appealed to all stakeholders to support the committee’s activities and urged road users to make road safety a shared responsibility. He said the Assembly remained committed to working with relevant institutions and communities to promote safer roads and reduce preventable road crashes in the Amansie West District.

items.title: Tchad : le président de la République ordonné le recrutement de 500 paramédicaux
items.description: © (DR) Ce lundi 24 août 2026 au Palais Toumaï, Mahamat Idriss Deby Itno, président de la République a présidé la reprise de la « Réunion du 24», consacrée au secteur de la santé. Pour cette reprise, les échanges ont été axés sur la vaccination, dont la couverture est passée de 41 % en 2017 à 71 % en 2025, avec un objectif de 90 % d’ici 2029. Des instructions ont été données par le chef de l'État afin de sécuriser le financement de la vaccination, d'apurer les engagements financiers envers les partenaires et de renforcer les ressources humaines, notamment avec le recrutement de 500 paramédicaux et l’intégration à la fonction publique de 226 agents arrivant en fin de contrat avec les partenaires. D'après le service de presee, avec la réactivation de la « Réunion du 24 », le président de la République entend installer un mécanisme régulier de suivi du secteur de la santé. La vaccination, choisie comme thème de cette première session, donne le ton: protection des enfants, prévention des épidémies et amélioration des performances sanitaires. L’article Tchad : le président de la République ordonné le recrutement de 500 paramédicaux est apparu en premier sur Journal du Tchad .

items.title: DG limogé, locaux vidés, projet de fusion … vers une disparition en catimini de la SING SA ?
items.description: Dix ans après sa création dans le cadre du projet eGabon financé par la Banque mondiale, la Société d’incubation numérique du Gabon (SING SA) semble traverser une zone de fortes turbulences. Son directeur général, Yannick Ebibie Nze, aurait été limogé à l’issue d’un récent conseil d’administration, alors qu’il se trouvait en séjour personnel en France. Dans le même temps, des interrogations se multiplient autour de l’avenir de la société, dont les locaux du centre-ville auraient été vidés, tandis qu’un projet de fusion avec le Centre gabonais de l’innovation (CGI) serait à l’étude au ministère de l’Économie numérique. Simple réorganisation ou disparition programmée de la SING SA ? Le directeur général de la SING SA, Yannick Ebibie Nze, a été limogé à l’issue d’un récent conseil d’administration. © D.R. Les derniers jours n’ont rien d’ordinaire du côté de la Société d’incubation numérique du Gabon. Selon des sources concordantes, un conseil d’administration récemment réuni pendant deux jours aurait décidé de mettre un terme aux fonctions de Yannick Ebibie Nze, directeur général de la SING SA depuis 2018. Une décision pour le moins surprenante dans sa forme, puisque l’intéressé se trouvait alors en France, dans le cadre d’un séjour personnel. Si son départ semble désormais acté, son successeur n’aurait, à ce jour, pas encore officiellement pris ses fonctions. En attendant, l’intérim serait assuré par Cyrille Ndong, nommé directeur général adjoint de la Société du patrimoine et des infrastructures numériques (SPIN) en janvier 2024. Un choix qui n’est pas anodin : la SPIN détient 30 % du capital de la SING SA pour le compte de l’État gabonais. Ce limogeage intervient surtout dans un contexte où des bruits persistants font état d’une profonde remise à plat du dispositif public d’accompagnement de l’innovation numérique. Des locaux vidés, une nouvelle adresse introuvable Comme si le départ du directeur général ne suffisait pas à alimenter les interrogations, un curieux ballet aurait été observé ces derniers jours au siège de la SING SA, au centre-ville de Libreville. Sur place, les locaux n’abriteraient plus les services de la société depuis environ une semaine. Un informateur rencontré sur les lieux affirme que la structure aurait déménagé. Mais vers quelle destination ? Mystère. Aucune nouvelle adresse officielle ne semble pour l’heure avoir été communiquée. Une situation pour le moins inhabituelle pour une société qui, depuis sa création, s’est précisément employée à se présenter comme l’un des principaux instruments de structuration de l’écosystème numérique gabonais. Et c’est ici que les interrogations prennent une autre dimension. Vers une fusion avec le CGI ? Selon plusieurs indiscrétions, l’avenir de la SING SA pourrait désormais se jouer autour du Centre gabonais de l’innovation (CGI), placé sous la tutelle du ministère de l’Économie numérique. Le scénario d’une fusion entre les deux structures serait actuellement sur la table. À défaut d’une simple mutualisation des moyens, l’hypothèse d’une concentration des activités au sein du CGI laisserait entrevoir, à terme, la disparition pure et simple de la SING SA. Le CGI, présenté comme un « hub d’innovation et de technologie dédié à l’émergence d’un écosystème numérique performant au Gabon » , semble en effet bénéficier d’un intérêt croissant de la part des pouvoirs publics. La structure, dirigée par Stéphane Nzeng, pourrait ainsi devenir le principal, voire l’unique véhicule public consacré à l’innovation et à l’accompagnement des entreprises technologiques. Dès lors, une question se pose : que deviendrait la SING SA et ses actifs dans un tel schéma ? Le mobilier qui se trouvait au siège du centre-ville aurait-il été transféré vers les installations du CGI, à la Rue des Résidences, à Batterie 4 ? Rien ne permet, pour l’heure, de l’affirmer. Une structure pourtant présentée comme un succès La perspective d’une disparition de la SING SA peut surprendre au regard du bilan revendiqué par la société depuis le démarrage effectif de ses activités en 2018. Issue du projet eGabon, financé par un prêt contracté par l’État gabonais auprès de la Banque mondiale, la SING SA devait contribuer à structurer l’économie numérique nationale. Le projet initial prévoyait la mise en place de trois incubateurs numériques dans les provinces de l’Estuaire, du Haut-Ogooué et de l’Ogooué-Maritime. Dans les faits, seule la structure de l’Estuaire a vu le jour. La société avait notamment pour mission de réduire les risques d’échec des projets de transformation digitale, d’accompagner les jeunes pousses technologiques et de favoriser l’émergence d’un écosystème numérique local. Son dispositif reposait sur quatre principaux leviers : l’incubation et l’accélération des startups à travers le programme Pivot 4.0, le conseil en stratégie d’innovation, l’ingénierie numérique avec sa Digital Factory, ainsi que l’accompagnement au financement et à la levée de fonds via SING Capital. Selon les données communiquées par l’écosystème numérique gabonais et le ministère de l’Économie numérique, plus de 314 startups auraient été accompagnées depuis 2018, dont environ 75 % des startups considérées comme les plus marquantes du pays. Près de 550 millions de FCFA auraient par ailleurs été mobilisés au profit des entrepreneurs. La SING SA revendique également un taux de survie post-incubation de 68 % pour les startups deux à trois ans après leur sortie de programme. Un bilan qui pose une autre question : si les résultats sont aussi significatifs, pourquoi envisager aujourd’hui de mettre fin à la structure qui les a produits ? Des signes avant-coureurs ? Le départ de Yannick Ebibie Nze ne serait, à en croire certaines sources, que l’aboutissement d’une séquence plus longue. Des indiscrétions font état de pressions exercées depuis plusieurs mois sur le désormais ex-directeur général. Son éviction n’aurait donc pas constitué une surprise pour certains observateurs proches du dossier. Surtout, le contexte institutionnel semble avoir changé. Créée dans le prolongement d’un projet financé par la Banque mondiale, la SING SA évolue désormais dans un environnement où l’État cherche à rationaliser ses instruments numériques et à éviter les chevauchements entre structures publiques. Dans cette logique, le rapprochement avec le CGI pourrait être présenté comme une volonté de rationalisation. Mais une fusion qui aboutirait à la suppression de la SING SA constituerait tout de même un changement majeur pour un dispositif qui aura fonctionné pendant près d’une décennie. Dix ans après, quel avenir pour la SING ? L’histoire de la SING SA est d’autant plus singulière que sa création n’a pas été exempte de difficultés. Deux ans avant le démarrage effectif de ses activités, un directeur général avait déjà été nommé. Mais celui-ci n’aurait manifestement pas rempli les missions qui lui étaient assignées, conduisant finalement au lancement d’un appel à candidatures pour son remplacement. Yannick Ebibie Nze avait alors été recruté à l’issue de cette procédure en 2018, au moment où la structure commençait réellement ses activités. Huit ans plus tard, son départ intervient alors que les indices d’une profonde réorganisation se multiplient : conseil d’administration décisif, direction générale vacante, intérim assuré par un responsable de la SPIN, locaux libérés et nouvelle adresse inconnue. À cela s’ajoute l’hypothèse d’une fusion avec le CGI, qui pourrait transformer radicalement le paysage institutionnel de l’innovation numérique au Gabon. Pour l’heure, aucune communication officielle ne permet de confirmer que la SING SA est appelée à disparaître. Mais les éléments concordants recueillis autour de son fonctionnement et de son devenir nourrissent une hypothèse désormais difficile à écarter : dix ans après sa création, la fin du projet SING semble avoir sonné. Reste à savoir si cette disparition annoncée répond à une véritable stratégie de rationalisation de l’écosystème numérique national ou si elle traduit l’échec d’un dispositif pourtant présenté comme l’un des fleurons de l’accompagnement des startups gabonaises. Affaire à suivre. L’article DG limogé, locaux vidés, projet de fusion … vers une disparition en catimini de la SING SA ? est apparu en premier sur Gabonreview.com | Actualité du Gabon | .

items.title: NLA urges local union to halt strike, return to negotiation table over pay dispute
items.description: The management of the National Lottery Authority (NLA) has issued an urgent call to its local staff union and workforce to immediately call off their sit-down strike and demonstration, urging employees to resume negotiations over an ongoing wage dispute that has led to industrial action. The appeal follows media coverage and growing public attention surrounding the labour impasse, which escalated when staff initiated a sit-down strike on Monday, August 24. In a press statement issued on Monday, August 24, 2026, and signed by the board and management, the Authority reaffirmed its commitment to resolving the impasse peacefully while outlining the financial context that influenced its salary offer. The Root Cause: Unpaid Tax Arrears & Net Pay Adjustments Management clarified that while the local union demanded a 17 per cent salary increase for 2026, the Authority granted a 12 per cent increase. According to management, this decision was directly tied to intervention regarding historical tax liabilities owed to the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA). The GRA notified the NLA of a backlog of unpaid income taxes on staff salaries covering six years from 2016 to 2022 , stemming from an incorrect tax application. “After several meetings with the GRA, the board and management entered into an arrangement with the GRA to pay the tax arrears totalling over five million Ghana cedis at no cost to Staff,” the statement revealed. To prevent further liabilities, the board and management agreed to rectify the anomaly by applying appropriate statutory taxes to salaries going forward. However, this adjustment reduced staff net takeaway salaries, prompting the Union to request a 17 per cent increment to cushion workers against the shortfall. Budgetary Constraints and Salary Negotiations During budgetary approvals, the board noted that because it had already absorbed over GH¢5 million in tax arrears alongside other budgetary constraints, it could initially approve only a 10 per cent salary increment. Management subsequently advocated for an additional 2 per cent, bringing the final offer to 12 per cent. The union rejected the 12 per cent offer, declared a deadlock, and forwarded the matter to the National Labour Commission (NLC) for redress. On Friday, August 21, the Union officially served management with notice of its intention to commence a sit-down strike and demonstration on Monday, August 24. Fair Wages Commission Recommendation & Ongoing Arbitration The statement also revealed that management had earlier written to the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC) on February 11, 2026, seeking guidance. In its response dated June 11, 2026, the FWSC advised the Authority to increase salaries by 8 per cent, based on the NLA’s current financial capacity, 4 percentage points below management’s offer of 12 per cent. Management affirmed that it is actively engaging the National Labour Commission (NLC) to achieve an amicable resolution through formal arbitration. “Management wishes to assure its cherished patrons, Lotto Marketing Companies, Private Lotto Operators (PLOs), third-party collaborators, and all stakeholders that it remains fully committed to fulfilling its mandate to raise revenue for national development,” the statement concluded.

items.title: La búsqueda del empresario burgalés que cayó al mar desde su barco mientras pescaba con su mujer en el Mediterráneo
items.description: Juan José Mutilba lleva jubilado desde 2021 y desde entonces se escapa cuando puede con su barco en viajes en los que también practicaba la pesca, una de sus pasiones. La última elección de este empresario burgalés de 66 años, cuya compañía suministra bidones de agua para los trabajadores de oficinas o puestos de trabajo, fue un recorrido por el mar Mediterráneo, entre la costa de Sicilia (Italia) y Grecia. El hombre permanece desaparecido desde el pasado martes tras resbalar en su embarcación y caer al agua sin que su esposa, que lo acompañaba, pudiera rescatarlo cuando quedó a la deriva ni avisar a las emergencias hasta tres días después del accidente porque no tenía cobertura. Las autoridades italianas buscan al burgalés mientras su familia ruega dedicación por si lograran localizarlo pese a la complejidad de estas actuaciones marítimas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Sanguié/Immersion patriotique obligatoire : les appelés mettent la main à la pâte à Faso-Mêbo
items.description: BURKINA-SANGUIE-REO-FASO-MEBO-IPO-APPELES-TRAVAUX Sanguié/Immersion patriotique obligatoire : les appelés mettent la main à la pâte à Faso-Mêbo Réo, 24 août 2026 (AIB) – Les appelés à l’Immersion patriotique obligatoire (IPO), session 2026, ont effectué le dimanche 23 août 2026, une demi-journée de travaux communautaires sur le site de Faso-Mêbo dans la province du Sanguié. Cette activité a permis aux jeunes de mettre en pratique les valeurs de civisme, de patriotisme et de responsabilité inculquées au cours de leur séjour d’immersion qui tire vers sa fin. Accompagnés de leurs encadreurs, les appelés ont participé activement aux travaux sur le site de Faso-Mêbo Sanguié. Au programme figuraient notamment le déplacement et la confection de pavés ainsi que le nettoyage du site. Une participation qui, selon la directrice provinciale de l’Enseignement secondaire et de la Formation professionnelle et technique du Sanguié, Rasmata Grâce Guingané, traduit la volonté de faire des jeunes, des acteurs de la construction nationale. « Ils sont des appelés, ils doivent aussi contribuer à la construction de la nation », a-t-elle expliqué, soulignant que la présence des jeunes sur le site de Faso-Mêbo répond à une orientation visant à rapprocher les appelés des initiatives concrètes de développement. La responsable provinciale s’est dite satisfaite de l’enthousiasme manifesté par les jeunes. Pour elle, l’IPO ne se limite pas aux enseignements théoriques. Les activités de reboisement, l’entretien quotidien des lieux de résidence et désormais la participation aux travaux de Faso-Mêbo constituent autant d’occasions de développer chez les jeunes le sens du devoir et de la responsabilité. Le coordonnateur adjoint de Faso-Mêbo Sanguié, l'adjudant de police Hermann Bado, a, pour sa part, salué la mobilisation des appelés. Il s’est dit honoré et fier de les accueillir sur le chantier et les a remerciés pour leur dynamique contribution. Il a également invité les autres élèves actuellement en vacances à venir, eux aussi, apporter leur contribution aux travaux de Faso-Mêbo. Pour Bama Léon Junior, appelé à l’IPO session 2026, cette participation traduit une conviction du camarade capitaine Ibrahim Traoré qu'il cite comme suit : le développement du Burkina Faso doit être porté par sa jeunesse. « Personne d’autre ne viendra développer notre nation », avant de rappeler les différentes activités auxquelles les appelés ont déjà pris part, notamment le reboisement et l’assainissement de leur cadre de vie. Le jeune appelé a reconnu qu’au début, l’immersion pouvait être perçue comme une contrainte. Mais au fil des jours, les enseignements reçus et les activités pratiques lui ont permis de mieux comprendre la vision de l’initiative. Il se considère désormais comme un « Burkinabè nouveau », prêt à servir sa patrie. À l’approche de la rentrée scolaire, Bama Léon Junior invite ses camarades à s’impliquer dans l’assainissement de leurs établissements et à s’organiser pour participer aux travaux de Faso-Mêbo. Pour lui, chaque geste compte dans la construction d’un Burkina Faso plus propre et plus prospère. Agence d'information du Burkina FGB/AS/ATA

items.title: Code de procédure civile : Ce que change la loi 58.25 entrée en vigueur ce lundi
items.description: Le Maroc a officiellement tourné, lundi 24 août, une page majeure de son organisation judiciaire avec l’entrée en vigueur de la loi n° 58.25 relative à la procédure civile. Ce nouveau texte remplace le dahir portant loi n° 1.74.447, qui encadrait les procédures civiles depuis plus de cinq décennies, et inaugure une réforme présentée comme l’un des chantiers structurants de la modernisation de la justice marocaine. Le législateur entend répondre aux limites révélées par l’application du précédent dispositif, souvent critiqué pour la complexité de ses mécanismes, la lenteur des procédures, les difficultés entourant la notification des actes et l’exécution des jugements, ainsi que pour l’intégration encore limitée des outils numériques dans la gestion des contentieux. La réforme ambitionne également de clarifier les règles relatives à la compétence des juridictions, aux voies de recours et aux modalités d’exécution des décisions judiciaires. Parmi les évolutions notables figure le renforcement du rôle du ministère public dans la préservation de l’ordre public au sein du contentieux civil. La nouvelle loi lui confère la faculté d’exercer un recours en nullité contre toute décision susceptible de porter atteinte à cet ordre public, y compris lorsqu’il n’était pas partie à l’instance initiale. Dans certaines situations particulières, il est par ailleurs dispensé du respect des délais de recours habituellement applicables. Le texte introduit également des mécanismes destinés à limiter les abus du droit d’agir en justice. Les juridictions peuvent désormais condamner l’auteur d’une procédure jugée abusive au versement de dommages-intérêts. Des sanctions financières sont aussi prévues lorsque les recours ou les oppositions sont considérés comme de simples moyens de retarder l’exécution des décisions de justice. Pour ses promoteurs, cette réforme vise avant tout à simplifier le parcours judiciaire des justiciables, à réduire les lourdeurs procédurales et à limiter ce qui est qualifié de « gaspillage procédural ». L’objectif affiché est d’assurer un traitement plus rapide, plus fluide et plus efficace des litiges devant les différentes juridictions du Royaume. La loi poursuit également un objectif d’harmonisation en réunissant dans un même texte les règles procédurales applicables aux contentieux civils, administratifs et commerciaux relevant de la justice de proximité. Cette orientation est présentée comme une traduction concrète des principes d’unité de la justice et de spécialisation des juridictions. Dans cette architecture renouvelée, les tribunaux de première instance deviennent compétents pour connaître des affaires civiles, sociales et familiales. Les sections spécialisées administratives et commerciales intégrées à ces juridictions sont, quant à elles, chargées de statuer sur les litiges relevant de leurs domaines respectifs. Le nouveau Code apporte également des précisions en matière de compétence judiciaire internationale. Il définit les situations dans lesquelles les juridictions marocaines peuvent être saisies de différends présentant un caractère international, en s’appuyant sur les principes contemporains du droit international privé. Cette évolution est présentée comme un levier destiné à renforcer la sécurité juridique et à améliorer l’attractivité du Maroc auprès des investisseurs. Concernant les conditions d’introduction des actions en justice, la réforme réaffirme l’obligation d’inscrire les affaires dans un registre dédié selon leur ordre chronologique de dépôt. Cet enregistrement doit comporter l’identité des parties, celle de leurs avocats lorsqu’ils sont constitués, l’objet du litige ainsi que la date de convocation. En matière d’assistance judiciaire, la loi prévoit que les recours dirigés contre les décisions de refus soient transmis à la juridiction de second degré dans un délai de huit jours à compter du dépôt de la requête, conformément aux dispositions de l’article 43. Le texte met également l’accent sur le développement des modes alternatifs de règlement des différends. Il consacre le rôle du juge dans la promotion des solutions amiables et autorise le tribunal à proposer une conciliation à n’importe quel stade de la procédure. Lorsqu’un accord intervient, celui-ci est consigné dans une décision insusceptible de recours. L’un des volets les plus importants de la réforme concerne la numérisation de la justice. Un chapitre entier est consacré à la digitalisation des procédures et des actes judiciaires. Le législateur ouvre notamment la possibilité de déposer requêtes, mémoires et recours à travers des plateformes électroniques unifiées et sécurisées. Il généralise également l’usage de la signature électronique et des échanges dématérialisés de documents, tout en prévoyant des garanties techniques destinées à assurer la protection des données personnelles et la valeur probante des procédures numériques. Dans cette même logique, la notification électronique acquiert une reconnaissance juridique pleine et entière. Les correspondances adressées aux comptes professionnels des avocats bénéficient désormais d’une force probante reconnue par la loi. Le texte prévoit en outre le recours à la carte nationale d’identité électronique comme référence subsidiaire lorsque la notification à l’adresse déclarée s’avère impossible. Les personnes morales de droit public sont tenues de communiquer leurs adresses électroniques, tandis que les personnes physiques et morales du secteur privé peuvent choisir ce mode de notification. Le nouveau Code introduit enfin plusieurs changements dans le domaine du référé et de l’exécution des décisions judiciaires. Il permet au juge de statuer sans convoquer la partie adverse dans les situations d’extrême urgence et fixe à quinze jours le délai d’appel des ordonnances de référé. Au stade de l’exécution, les pouvoirs du juge de l’exécution sont renforcés. La réforme autorise également le recours à une plateforme numérique pour identifier les biens du débiteur et suivre l’avancement des procédures, tout en ouvrant la possibilité de procéder à des ventes par voie électronique. L’entrée en vigueur de ce nouveau cadre procédural a été précédée par plusieurs circulaires émanant du Conseil supérieur du pouvoir judiciaire, du ministère de la Justice et de l’Agence judiciaire du Royaume. Ces documents ont apporté des précisions et des orientations destinées à accompagner la mise en œuvre des nombreuses innovations introduites par cette réforme de grande ampleur. The post Code de procédure civile : Ce que change la loi 58.25 entrée en vigueur ce lundi appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Four arrested over murder of South African boxing champion Zolani Tete
items.description: Police in South Africa have taken four individuals into custody following the fatal shooting of former world boxing champion Zolani Tete. The thirty-eight-year-old athlete was killed outside his residence in Mdantsane, located in the Eastern Cape province. Authorities confirmed that the ambush occurred on Thursday evening as Tete waited for his property gate to open. Two armed assailants wearing balaclavas emerged from another vehicle and opened fire on his car. A twenty-seven-year-old female passenger sustained serious gunshot wounds during the attack and remains hospitalised. Judicial Proceedings and Police Investigation Law enforcement agencies moved swiftly over the weekend to apprehend four suspects ranging in age from twenty-two to twenty-eight. A twenty-two-year-old man arrested on Saturday faces initial charges of murder and attempted murder during his court appearance. Three additional suspects were arrested on Sunday, with two facing preliminary charges for the unlawful possession of firearms and ammunition. Investigators continue to review evidence to determine whether murder charges will apply to all detained individuals. An Illustrious Athletic Career Tete established a formidable reputation in international boxing through multiple world championship victories and record-breaking performances. He captured the International Boxing Federation junior-bantamweight title in 2014 before claiming the World Boxing Organisation bantamweight crown three years later. In 2017, he set a Guinness World Record for the fastest knockout in a championship bout by defeating challenger Siboniso Gonya in just eleven seconds. His professional record included twenty-nine victories across thirty-four fights. Controversy and Comeback Ambitions His career faced a significant setback when a subsequent victory in the United Kingdom was invalidated following a positive test for the anabolic steroid stanozolol. The UK Anti-Doping Agency subsequently imposed a four-year suspension that concluded in late July. Manager Mla Tengimfene noted that Tete was actively preparing for a professional return to the ring. Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie lamented the abrupt end to his athletic ambitions. “South Africa has lost one of the finest fighters it has ever produced,” McKenzie stated. “He was training for a return to the ring. He believed he still had something to give this country. He was right, but he will not get the chance now. He, and all of us, have been robbed.” Former Sports Minister Fikile Mbalula also offered condolences, remembering him as a great national contributor to the sport. As investigations continue and the judicial process unfolds, the tragic loss of a celebrated sporting figure underscores the profound impact of violent crime on communities striving to reclaim their safety and honour their local heroes.

items.title: UG students urged to acquire practical skills to drive AfCFTA implementation across Africa
items.description: University of Ghana students have been urged to acquire the practical skills needed to drive the implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). The call was made at the launch of the 2026 GITFiC AfCFTA Tertiary Students’ Week, a three-day programme aimed at exposing students to the opportunities and practical demands of Africa’s single market. The programme is being held under the theme “Empowering the Next Generation to Learn, Connect, Trade, Innovate and Lead.” President of the University of Ghana Chapter of the GITFiC AfCFTA Tertiary Students’ Club, Adu Boahen Felix, said Africa’s challenge is no longer the absence of a trade agreement but the lack of skilled professionals capable of implementing it. “Africa does not have a trade agreement problem. Africa has a trade capacity problem,” he said. He explained that the successful implementation of AfCFTA would require professionals who understand how to price cross-border transactions, apply rules of origin, navigate customs procedures, finance and insure shipments, and build businesses capable of operating across multiple African markets. He said universities must therefore play a central role in equipping students with these skills before they enter the job market. Mr Boahen described current university students as the “implementation generation” of AfCFTA, arguing that they will ultimately be responsible for moving goods, negotiating contracts and building businesses across the continent. AfCFTA club expands He disclosed that the GITFiC AfCFTA Tertiary Students’ Club, which was established at the University of Ghana in March 2023, has since expanded to the University for Development Studies, All Nations University and the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology. A chapter has also been established at the University of Lome in Togo. Under the GITFiC Agenda 2031 , the club aims to establish chapters in at least 100 tertiary institutions across Africa by 2031. Mr Boahen also said a full AfCFTA curriculum for tertiary institutions has been developed, while a professional certificate programme on AfCFTA is available to students and working professionals. Students challenged to go beyond the classroom Vice President of the club, Doreen Amoatey Akweley, said the annual Students’ Week is designed to expose students to practical aspects of the African trade agenda. She said the programme would bring students into direct contact with industry players and create opportunities for them to connect with one another. “AfCFTA will only work if Africa develops the human capacity to operate the single market,” she said. She stressed the importance of understanding cross-border contracts, rules of origin, customs procedures, financing and insurance as part of the skills needed to make the agreement effective. ‘Africa’s transformation will not be driven from Geneva or New York’ Patron of the club, Professor Rosina Foli, challenged students and academics to take a more active role in shaping Africa’s trade future. She noted that AfCFTA has created a single market of about 1.4 billion people , but cautioned that the agreement alone would not transform the continent without the necessary human capacity and practical action. Prof. Foli said the GITFiC AfCFTA Tertiary Students’ Club serves as the academic extension of the Ghana International Trade and Finance Conference, bringing students from different disciplines together to develop and implement ideas around continental free trade. She said club members would also serve as Student Ambassadors for AfCFTA , with opportunities to participate in international conferences, regional seminars, forums and other structured programmes. Prof. Foli called for greater involvement of academia in the AfCFTA agenda, arguing that universities have not been sufficiently integrated into discussions about Africa’s economic transformation. She urged academics to help train the researchers, human resource professionals, industrialists, negotiators and scientists who will contribute to the continent’s economic development. Learn, connect and lead The Patron encouraged students to focus on three key areas — learning, connecting and leading . She urged them to deepen their understanding of the Protocol on Trade in Services, use the club to connect campus businesses and startups to AfCFTA opportunities, and take leadership roles in Africa’s economic transformation. “Africa’s economic transformation will not be driven from Geneva or New York. It will be driven from rooms like this at the University of Ghana,” she said. The 2026 Students’ Week will include a sports festival and a startup pitch competition, providing students with an opportunity to present business ideas to judges. Organisers are also calling on businesses and industry players to support students through internships, mentorship and other opportunities for practical experience in African trade. The Patron formally declared the GITFiC AfCFTA Tertiary Students’ Week 2026 launched, with a call on students to “Learn, Connect, Trade, Innovate and Lead” for Ghana and Africa.

items.title: Moody's lifts Pakistan sovereign rating to B3 from Caa1, cites improved governance and easing of external risk
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Global ratings agency Moody’s on Monday upgraded Pakistan’s sovereign credit rating to B3 from Caa1 and maintained a stable outlook, citing expectations of improvements in governance and easing external and fiscal vulnerabilities. “The upgrade to B3 reflects our expectations that improvements in governance will allow the government to sustain the recent improvements in the country’s external position and strengthen fiscal metrics,” Moody’s said in an announcement. Pakistan’s external vulnerability risks have eased further since its last rating action in August 2025 at Caa1, with foreign exchange reserves building steadily, supported by sustained macroeconomic stabilisation, it said. At the same time, lower domestic financing costs amid monetary easing and an improved fiscal position have driven a material improvement in Pakistan’s debt affordability, the US-based rating firms stated, adding that Pakistan’s strengthening credit profile is also demonstrating greater resilience to external shocks than in previous cycles, including the ongoing Middle East conflict. However, it warned that notwithstanding these improvements, Pakistan’s credit profile remained vulnerable due to a structurally fragile external position, weak debt affordability, a still relatively narrow revenue base and constraints on attracting investment and stimulating high-productivity and economic growth. These credit constraints are embedded in the B3 rating. The stable outlook balances a potentially faster improvement in Pakistan’s credit fundamentals against outstanding risks related to the vulnerabilities above, which, if materialised, could weaken access to foreign-currency financing and further reduce fiscal flexibility. The upgrade to B3 from Caa1 also applies to the backed foreign currency senior unsecured ratings for The Pakistan Global Sukuk Programme Co Ltd, the agency said. The associated payment obligations are direct obligations of the Pakistan’s government. The outlook for Pakistan Global Sukuk Programme Co Ltd remains stable, it said. Concurrent to today’s action, Moody’s also raised Pakistan’s local and foreign currency country ceilings to B1 and B3, from B2 and Caa1 respectively. The two-notch gap between the local currency ceiling and sovereign rating is driven by the government’s relatively large footprint in the economy, weak institutions, and high political and external vulnerability risk. The two-notch gap between the foreign currency ceiling and the local currency ceiling reflects incomplete capital account convertibility and relatively weak policy effectiveness. It also takes into account risks of transfer and convertibility restrictions being imposed. The rating agency noted that foreign exchange reserves increased to about $17 billion at end-July 2026, from $14bn in end-July 2025, sufficient to cover nearly three months of imports. As such, Pakistan’s External Vulnerability Indicator (the ratio of short-term and long-term maturing debt to foreign exchange reserves) has improved to about 145 per cent in 2026, compared to 230pc in 2025. Continued implementation of the IMF-supported reform programme has strengthened policy credibility, maintained macroeconomic stabilisation and underpinned financing from official creditors. Pakistan has also regained gradual access to market financing, including a three-year, $750 million Eurobond issued in April 2026 and a CNY 1.75bn (about $250m) debut Panda bond in May 2026. Together, these developments have enabled an accumulation of reserves while allowing Pakistan to meet all of its external obligations in FY26. Moody’s expected foreign exchange reserves to rise to about $19-20bn at the end of fiscal 2027 and $20-21bn in FY28, subject to the government’s sustained progress on the IMF programme, enabling timely disbursements from official partners and continued gradual access to market financing. In turn, continued adherence to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme would allow Pakistan to meet its external financing needs of about $21bn in fiscal 2027 and around $30bn in fiscal 2028, according to IMF estimates, while supporting continued reserves accumulation. About $7bn and $12bn of financing requirements in FY27 and FY28, respectively, comprise existing bilateral deposits, expected to be rolled over. Yet, Pakistan’s external position remains vulnerable to shocks, particularly given still-large external financing requirements, it noted. However, the projected reserve accumulation provides a larger buffer than in recent years against adverse market or commodity-price developments, including the elevated oil prices associated with the ongoing Middle East conflict, the statement said. Pakistan’s debt affordability has also improved materially, from very weak levels. Interest payments absorbed about 35pc of government revenue in fiscal 2026, down sharply from 49pc in fiscal 2025. The rating agency expected the recent improvement in Pakistan’s debt affordability to be durable, underpinned by sustained macroeconomic stability. While inflation remains sensitive to exchange-rate movements and external shocks, improved external buffers, a more stable macroeconomic environment and the authorities’ commitment to fiscal consolidation should help contain inflationary pressures and support debt affordability gains. Although higher global energy prices stemming from geopolitical tensions pose upside risks to inflation, Moody’s expected Pakistan’s strengthened policy framework and improved economic resilience to mitigate their impact.

items.title: Lélouma : à la découverte de Tunti Malaande, cette roche insolite qui défie les lois de l’équilibre à Ley-Hoolo
items.description: « À mon arrivée ici, je me suis tout d’abord demandé comment cette grosse roche pouvait tenir ainsi. C’est tout simplement gigantesque, impressionnant et spectaculaire. » Made with LogoLicious Add Your Logo App À moins de deux kilomètres du district de Ley-Hoolo, dans la sous-préfecture de Korbé, à Lélouma, se dresse une formation rocheuse aussi spectaculaire qu’insolite. Baptisée Tunti Malaande , qui signifie littéralement « la roche épargnée », cette curiosité naturelle attire progressivement l’attention des habitants, des visiteurs et des amoureux de la nature. Sa silhouette particulière évoque, selon l’angle sous lequel on l’observe, tantôt un gigantesque champignon, tantôt un parapluie suspendu dans le vide. Dressée au cœur d’un paysage montagneux remarquable, la roche offre un décor qui ne laisse pas indifférent. Aujourd’hui, Tunti Malaande est devenue un lieu de passage pour les curieux, les amateurs de photographie et les visiteurs à la recherche de sites naturels atypiques. Pourtant, le potentiel touristique de cet endroit reste encore largement inexploité. Boubacar Siddy Diallo, ancien conseiller de la mairie de Korbé et natif de Ley-Hoolo, se réjouit de voir ce site gagner progressivement en notoriété. « Nous sommes ici à Tunti Malaande, cette magnifique roche qui fait parler de notre district depuis un bon bout de temps. La médiatisation de ce lieu a commencé avec notre association, qui l’avait utilisée comme légende. Ensuite, avec l’émergence des réseaux sociaux, Tunti Malaande s’est fait de plus en plus connaître. C’est un plaisir pour moi, en tant que natif de la localité. Aujourd’hui, même des étrangers viennent ici pour voir cette pierre », se réjouit-il. Une œuvre façonnée par la nature Ici, nul architecte ni ingénieur. C’est la nature qui a façonné ce décor au fil du temps. L’érosion, les caractéristiques géologiques de la roche et les phénomènes naturels ont progressivement donné à cette formation son apparence singulière. Pour les visiteurs, le résultat est tout simplement spectaculaire Made with LogoLicious Add Your Logo App « À mon arrivée ici, je me suis tout d’abord demandé comment cette grosse roche pouvait tenir ainsi. C’est tout simplement gigantesque, impressionnant et spectaculaire », s’étonne Amadou Lama Diallo. Revenant sur l’origine de l’appellation et sur l’importance que revêt ce lieu pour les habitants, le doyen explique : « si vous entendez “Tunti”, sachez que cela signifie la roche et “Malaande”, épargnée. Du coup, l’endroit mérite bien son nom de “roche épargnée”. Parce que cette structure, seul le Bon Dieu sait comment il a pu la réaliser de cette manière. La roche en question est suspendue sur d’autres roches qui lui servent de fondation et elle surplombe tout l’alentour. Elle est soutenue par une autre roche plus fine. C’est très impressionnant », explique-t-il. Selon lui, la formation rocheuse offre également un espace naturel particulièrement agréable. « Sous cette roche, même une centaine de personnes peuvent s’abriter de la pluie ou du soleil sans être impactées. En plus, quelle que soit la chaleur, un vent humide souffle sous la roche. D’ici, on peut également observer tout l’environnement avec un magnifique paysage », souligne-t-il. Un potentiel touristique à valoriser Malgré son caractère exceptionnel, Tunti Malaande ne bénéficie pour l’heure d’aucun aménagement spécifique. Le site reste difficilement exploitable sur le plan touristique et certains comportements des visiteurs et des riverains posent également problème. Selon les témoignages recueillis sur place, des visiteurs indélicats laissent parfois ouverts les portails des villages, permettant à des animaux de pénétrer dans les champs et d’endommager les cultures. Le défi est donc désormais de parvenir à préserver et à valoriser ce patrimoine naturel, tout en créant les conditions nécessaires à son exploitation touristique. Avec ses formes étonnantes, son paysage montagneux et son histoire locale, Tunti Malaande pourrait, à terme, devenir l’un des sites naturels les plus emblématiques de Lélouma et une véritable opportunité de développement pour la localité.
